item.content:encoded:
When Aaron Judge is healthy, he’s the most dangerous hitter in baseball. Sometimes I get alarmed at how uncontroversial a statement that is; ours is a sport that so frequently humiliates those who make such sweeping, unequivocal judgments as those.
But the empirical evidence is what it is. Judge has played 150 or more games in a season four times in his career. In those four seasons, he’s led all position players in WAR four times and led the league in wRC+ three times. He’s been named AL MVP three times and finished second once, ahead of some real doozies: Cal Raleigh’s 60-homer year, Bobby Witt Jr.’s 10.5-WAR campaign in 2024, Shohei Ohtani’s best pitching season — in fact, a healthy Judge is the only thing that’s ever trumped a healthy Ohtani in an MVP race.
So again, it’s not uncontroversial to say that when Judge is healthy he’s the best hitter in the world. He has not, however, always been healthy. Least of all this season, when he missed three months with a broken rib. And now, the single-season AL home run king is back on the IL with a calf strain. The timing could not be worse.
Judge last played on Wednesday, leaving open the option to activate him on Sunday for the final game of the regular season. That seems like a theoretical concern at the moment rather than a practical one. Our Matt Martell was at Yankee manager Aaron Boone’s pregame media availability on Tuesday morning, where Boone illustrated the inadequacy of a return-to-play timeline at this point in the season.
“We’re planning on [Judge] not being a part of [the Wild Card Series],” Boone said. “You hear all the time with injuries, we give ranges: two to four weeks, four to six. They’re ranges for a reason. We’re at a point in the year where, obviously, we’d push it a little bit if that was in play, but that’s a week away. I’m not expecting it, but I’m not ruling it out either.”
That’s the problem. A range of two weeks in recovery time isn’t a big deal in a six-month season, but even one week is twice as long as the Yankees’ entire first playoff round. And muscle injuries can be finicky to begin with — you go to bed one night feeling fine and wake up the next morning with weakness or stiffness.
For what it’s worth, the Yankees are technically still alive in the AL East race as of this writing, but you can forgive Boone for speaking as if the division is already lost.
Either way, in order to speed things along, Judge received a platelet-poor plasma (PPP) injection on Monday, not to be confused with a platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection.
Now, apparently having read The Magic School Bus Inside the Human Body as a child is not a sufficient qualification to perform surgery on live patients. At least, that’s what the police told me. But anyone who’s read that book can tell you the makeup of human blood: Red blood cells, which carry oxygen; white blood cells, which fight infection; platelets, which stop bleeding and heal wounds; and plasma, which is the broth all the other stuff floats around in.
PRP injections are a pretty common treatment for sports injuries, but taking the healing bits out of plasma seems kind of counterintuitive. Sort of like a vodka-poor screwdriver. But evidently PPP contains high levels of fibrinogen, which is itself a healing agent. Ms. Frizzle didn’t cover fibrinogen, but sure, I’ll buy it.
Unless the PPP works an actual miracle, though, it looks like the Yankees are going to have to navigate at least the first round of the playoffs without their best player.
And even if Judge does return — either in the Wild Card round or later, if the Yankees advance — I’d caution against assuming that we’d be seeing the best of him right off the proverbial bat. For starters, 99% of star athletes in history are going to try to force their way into the lineup for the playoffs regardless of whether they’re actually healthy.
To say nothing of the fact that Judge can be streaky. This is the nature of Judge’s unusual skill set; there are 1,073 hitters in major league history with at least 5,000 career plate appearances. Judge is the only one of those who’s produced one of the three true outcomes (home run, strikeout, walk) in more than half of his career plate appearances. (I’d like to express my immense gratitude to Adam Dunn, who has a career TTO% of 49.9, for making this fun fact possible.)
Living on the extremes, as he does, Judge will have weeks where he homers every night, and others where he goes 1-for-20 with 12 strikeouts. But you live with it because, over a long enough timeline, it works out heavily in his favor. Among hitters with at least 5,000 career plate appearances, Judge has the third-highest career wRC+, trailing only Babe Ruth and Ted Williams. If you wanted to go further than “best hitter now” and anoint Judge the best hitter ever, leaning heavily on the argument that quality of competition increases over time, you’d have a credible case.
But that’s not what the Yankees got out of Judge this year. In 66 regular-season games, he’s hit .241/.360/.511, with his highest strikeout rate (29.8%) since 2019 and lowest wRC+ (141) since 2020. In seven games since he returned from his rib injury, Judge was just 4-for-23 with one home run, one walk, and 13 strikeouts.
I’ve done enough of these injury reaction posts to figure out that they’re not really about the guy who got hurt, but about the teammates he’s leaving behind.
And I don’t want to underrate the value of Judge — even the version of Judge that has a 141 wRC+, rather than a 200 wRC+ — but the Yankees have done OK without him.
In the weakest American League field in decades, the Yankees are one of only two teams with a winning percentage of .550 or better. Entering their doubleheader with the Rays on Tuesday, the Yankees are still first in the AL in home runs (216) and second in runs scored per game (4.60). Even without Judge (or Giancarlo Stanton, for that matter), their lineup has plenty of beef.

Ben Rice in particular has been absolutely terrific this season. He’s fourth among qualified AL hitters in wRC+ and third in both home runs and runs scored. The Astros have AL MVP frontrunner Yordan Alvarez in their lineup; apart from him, is there any hitter in the AL bracket who’s been Rice’s equal this year? Maybe Junior Caminero? Willson Contreras, if you value OBP over raw power? Even if you’re being charitable, it’s a short list.
Now, past Rice, things get interesting, because if you want to talk about the Yankees’ offensive depth, you have to be able to hold multiple ideas in your head at once.
As of Tuesday morning, the Yankees have 11 hitters with double-digit home runs this season, which is tied for the most in the league. That’s just counting players who have hit 10 or more home runs in pinstripes, and the Yankees brought in substantial reinforcements midseason. Luis García Jr. has just seven homers for the Yankees but 30 overall. Heliot Ramos has four home runs in 32 games and 13 overall, with 20-plus in each of his previous two seasons. George Lombard Jr. has just five home runs in 37 major league games, but he hit 12 dingers in 78 minor league games before he got called up.
Count all this up and the Yankees have more hitters with at least decent pop than they can fit on the roster at once.
At the same time, Rice is the only Yankee with 20 home runs in pinstripes this year. So while this lineup is short on automatic outs, if Judge is out, there’s a massive drop-off after Rice.
If you take Judge out of the picture, Cody Bellinger is second on the Yankees in wRC+, at 119. The Rays don’t have anyone with 100 or more plate appearances and a better wRC+ than Rice this season, but they have four hitters (Caminero, Yandy Díaz, Jonathan Aranda, and Victor Mesa Jr.) with 100 or more plate appearances and a better wRC+ than Bellinger. So do the Rangers (Justin Foscue, Josh Jung, Joc Pederson, Wyatt Langford). The Astros have Alvarez, plus Isaac Paredes and Jeremy Peña. The White Sox have Miguel Vargas, Munetaka Murakami, and Tristan Peters.
As good as Rice has been, the Yankees’ lineup looks concerningly pedestrian without Judge. If you aren’t already a FanGraphs Member, please consider becoming one; it’s the only way to get trenchant original analysis like this.
The good news is that Judge’s calf injury runs counter to the rest of the team’s injury luck. Carlos Rodón, who missed almost three months with an elbow injury earlier this year, dominated the Rays in eight scoreless innings in Game 1 of a doubleheader on Tuesday. The same day, the Yankees activated Chisholm, who’d spent two weeks on the IL with a sprained thumb. Clarke Schmidt just returned from Tommy John surgery last week, and while he suffered biceps cramping in the bullpen on Sunday, it appears to be a minor setback. Trent Grisham remains a question mark for the start of the playoffs as he recovers from a hamstring injury, but his prognosis also looks good.
Judge is as important to the Yankees as any two or three other players put together, but with a healthy and deep rotation and Rice leading the way offensively, they’re not in bad shape. The remainder of this roster could easily survive and advance through a weaker AL bracket, setting the stage for a dramatically timed Judge return in mid-October. Like Kirk Gibson, only bigger.
Michael is a writer at FanGraphs. Previously, he was a staff writer at The Ringer and D1Baseball, and his work has appeared at Grantland, Baseball Prospectus, The Atlantic, ESPN.com, and various ill-remembered Phillies blogs. Follow him on Twitter, if you must, @MichaelBaumann.

item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge is out, and the Yankees don’t know when — or if — he’ll be back.
So if they’re going to go anywhere in the playoffs, they’ll almost certainly have to do some work without him.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
That means Cody Bellinger’s role will be even more important than it’s been for much of the season, and lately, he’s answered the call.
It was Bellinger’s two-run shot in Game 1 on Tuesday that provided all the scoring in the 2-0 win over Tampa Bay in The Bronx.
The blast was Bellinger’s 17th of the season and fifth in his past 12 games.
With Judge out indefinitely with a strained right calf, Aaron Boone said the team was “not expecting” Judge to be available for the wild-card series that begins next week.
As Bellinger said following the win in Tuesday’s opener, any chance the Yankees have without Judge will be due to a collective effort.
But there’s little doubt that Bellinger — whose $36.5 million salary this year is second only to Judge’s $40 million — will be called upon more than most.
Against right-hander Nick Martinez of Tampa Bay, Bellinger hit second — a spot that he and Ben Rice have mostly split in Judge’s absence.
Rice doubled off Martinez to lead off the bottom of the fourth of a scoreless game, and Bellinger followed with his shot out to right.
“[Rice] had a great at-bat in front of me [and] saw a lot of pitches,’’ Bellinger said. “It was a close game. I’m not trying to do too much at all. I want to keep it really simple, put a good swing on the ball.”
It’s the approach the Yankees are hoping to have without Judge, whose “moderate” strain has put their October plans in jeopardy.
“I think for us, it’s one game at a time,’’ Bellinger said. “We all believe in each other in this locker room. We’re not looking too far ahead.”
But it’s hard not to wonder how the lineup — and team — will withstand another Judge absence.
“Having Judge on our team helps us tremendously,’’ Bellinger said. “We’ve just got to continue to come out and win games, playing for each other, leaning on each other [and] playing good baseball.”
As the Yankees have noted, they’ve stayed in the postseason picture, even as Judge missed three-plus months with a fractured rib this summer.
Shop Yankees Merch
“We have a lot of talent in this locker room, a lot of depth,” Bellinger said. “A lot of different guys stepped up, whether it’s their first year in the big leagues or getting traded [here]. We keep playing winning baseball.”
Bellinger added to that not just with his bat Tuesday, but with his arm, as well.
After Victor Mesa Jr. opened the sixth with a single off Carlos Rodón, Bellinger started an inning-ending double play two batters later when Richie Palacios lined out to left.
Mesa didn’t know where the ball was and didn’t get back to first in time to beat Bellinger’s strong throw.
“He went through that stretch when he was struggling and then got injured,’’ Boone said of Bellinger’s earlier slump and hamstring injury. “But he’s dialed in now and hitting line drives all over the ballpark. … It’s good to see as we get down the stretch.”

item.content:encoded:
A week or two ago, Tuesday’s doubleheader loomed as perhaps the largest day (and night) of the Yankees season.
But the Rays separating themselves — entering with a six-game lead that had doubled since Sept. 11 — and requiring just one victory in this four-game set to clinch the division drained much of the drama from the opening game of the series at a half-filled Stadium.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
And so a strong afternoon effort by the Yankees encouraged and kept their AL East hopes alive, but it more kept those hopes on a ventilator than revive them.
In the first of two games on the day, the Yankees beat the Rays 2-0 in front of an announced crowd of 41,421 in The Bronx during a brisk late-September afternoon that hinted at October.
In all likelihood, also coming soon is the Rays wrapping up the division, but the Yankees (90-66) at least did not allow their rival to celebrate on their grass immediately. Of course, the Rays (95-61) have three more chances to do so, including another that was set for just a few hours later.
“We all believe in each other in this locker room and not looking too far ahead,” said Cody Bellinger, who provided the only run-scoring swing in the victory that clinched no worse than the top wild-card spot.
The Yankees are nearly guaranteed a first-round home date with the Red Sox in a best-of-three series that likely would not include their best player: The club is operating under the belief Aaron Judge will not be available for the series because of his calf strain.
If Aaron Boone’s bunch is going to escape the Red Sox and face off with these same Rays in the ALDS, they would have to rely on their stars rather than their superstar.
On that front, Tuesday afternoon provided some hope with Carlos Rodón (eight shutout, overpowering innings in which he faced just one over the minimum) and Bellinger (a two-run blast in the fourth inning that provided the only runs the club needed) stepping up.
“Just a really solid, quick win,” Boone said of a game that lasted just 2 hours, 2 minutes in large part because of Rodón’s dominance and efficiency, which bodes well for the postseason even if Rodón probably would not get a first-round start.
In his longest, best and likely last outing of the regular season, Rodón struck out eight and allowed just three base runners on three singles.
The first two were erased by double plays (the second, in the sixth inning, entailed Bellinger catching a Richie Palacios line drive and throwing strong to first to double up Victor Mesa Jr.).
The third was a one-out single to Jonathan Aranda in the seventh inning, which might have presented the greatest threat to Rodón. But against Junior Caminero — an MVP candidate who represented the tying run — the veteran reached back for his two hardest pitches of the game (both 97.5 mph fastballs) to get ahead 0-2 before finishing Caminero off with a slider.
“He was awesome. Strike throwing was great,” Boone said of Rodón, who needed 96 pitches to record 24 outs, won his 100th career game and tallied his 1,500th strikeout. “… [He had] velo when he really needed it.”
The Yankees offense was held down by Nick Martinez for three perfect innings before pouncing on two consecutive imperfect pitches to begin the bottom of the fourth.
Ben Rice roped a double down the right field line for the first Yankees hit before Bellinger got a first-pitch sinker across the middle of the plate and clubbed it to right for his 17th homer of the season.
And that was all Rodón needed in a game that might have given the club a blueprint for how it can succeed in October against a team like the Rays and without a monstrous presence like Judge.
“You see the defense today — we’re solid,” said Rodón, who praised José Caballero (a bunt single and two steals in an empty fifth inning) before addressing the rest of the club. “Some lengthy at-bats. Some big-time hits — the homer from Beli there. The bullpen is deep.
“The starters are really good. I have a lot of confidence in this club.”

item.content:encoded:
By Larry Fleisher
The Associated Press
NEW YORK — Yankees slugger Aaron Judge is unlikely to play in the Wild Card Series after having an injection in his sore right calf, manager Aaron Boone said Tuesday.
Before the Yankees faced the Rays in a day-night doubleheader, Boone said Judge had a platelet poor plasma injection during the team’s off-day on Monday following its return from Arizona.
“We’re planning on him not being a part of that (Wild Card Series) but we’re also at time of the year, you hear all the time with injuries, you give ranges two to four weeks, four to six weeks,” Boone said. “The range is for a reason and we’re at a point of the year where obviously we push it a little bit if that was in play but that’s a week away. I’m not expecting it, but I’m not ruling it out either.”
The Yankees will most likely play the Boston Red Sox in the first round of the postseason.
Judge was put on the 10-day injured list Saturday with a strained soleus muscle, which is in the lower part of his calf. Boone did not say what grade the strain is but described it as “moderate.”
Judge is eligible to be activated for the regular-season finale on Sunday against Baltimore but will not do much activity in the next few days.
Judge injured his calf during last Wednesday’s game at Minnesota. The eight-time All-Star was lifted in the sixth inning for a pinch hitter because of discomfort in his leg and said at the time it was a precautionary move.
Boone said symptoms persisted and an MRI revealed the strain.
Judge was 4 for 23 with 13 strikeouts and one extra-base hit in seven games after returning Sept. 8 from a broken rib, which kept him out of the lineup for more than three months.
Judge is hitting .241 with 18 homers and 41 RBIs in just 66 games this year. He hit a long homer on Sept. 14 in Minnesota and had the next game off before straining his calf.
The Yankees entered Tuesday with a 48-41 record in the games Judge has missed and a 41-25 mark in games he has played. New York also began Tuesday a loss away from being eliminated from the AL East race, setting up a second straight wild-card series against the Red Sox next week.
“We’ve played much of the year without him and for the most part, we’ve done a pretty good job,” Boone said. “So guys are used to it. Obviously you always want your best player in the mix, but we understand we’ve got a job to do and an expectation to win. I think that expectation doesn’t change with or without him. We’re expecting to go into the series and know we can beat anyone when we play our game.”

item.content:encoded:
Yankees de Nueva York jugarían la Ronda de Comodines de la MLB 2026 sin su capitán, Aaron Judge; esta es la razón
A la temporada regular de las Grandes Ligas aun le quedan 2 series para disputar por equipo, siendo el próximo martes 29 de septiembre cuando comiencen la Ronda de Comodines, en donde Yankees podría jugar sin Aaron Judge.
Los Yankees de Nueva York afrontarán posiblemente una eventual Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana ante los Medias Rojas de Boston sin su capitán, Aaron Judge.
El manager del equipo, Aaron Boone confirmó este martes 22 de septiembre que el equipo trabaja con el escenario de no contar con Judge, aunque dejó abierta la posibilidad de acelerar su recuperación si la situación lo requiere.
¿Por qué Aaron Judge no podría jugar la Ronda de Comodines con Yankees?
El beisbolista de estadounidense de 34 años sufrió una distensión de "grado moderado" en la pantorrilla derecha y tiene comprometida su presencia en el inicio de la postemporada.
Judge fue colocado el pasado sábado en la lista de lesionados de 10 días, con efecto retroactivo al 17 de septiembre, después de sufrir la distensión durante la serie de la semana pasada contra los Mellizos de Minnesota.
El toletero recibió el lunes una inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas y tendrá actividad limitada durante los próximos días. "El par de días siguientes no habrá mucho: nada de correr, saltar, cosas así", indicó Boone.
Judge explicó que la lesión afecta al músculo sóleo de la pantorrilla derecha, una zona que considera especialmente importante para correr y batear.
"He lidiado con distensiones antes y de alguna manera he jugado con ellas, pero esta fue en un lugar diferente donde lo hizo un poco más difícil", comentó Judge.
¿Cuánto tardaría en recuperarse Aaron Judge para volver a jugar con Yankees?
Una distensión de grado 2 en la pantorrilla suele requerir entre 3 y 6 semanas de recuperación, un plazo que complica su presencia en el comienzo de los playoffs.
"Si él es capaz de jugar, entonces le daremos esa oportunidad", señaló Boone.
Judge, que ya se perdió buena parte del verano por una fractura en la costilla derecha, apenas disputó siete partidos desde su regreso en septiembre.
En 66 encuentros esta campaña bateó .241/.360/.511, con 18 jonrones y 41 carreras impulsadas
Los Yankees ya aseguraron su boleto a los playoffs, pero una victoria de los Rays de Tampa Bay en cualquiera de los encuentros de la doble cartelera de este martes 22 de septiembre les permitiría conquistar el Este de la Liga Americana y el primer sembrado de la liga, lo que enviaría a Nueva York a disputar la Serie del Comodín.
Yankees Manager Aaron Boone said today that the team is not planning on Aaron Judge being available for the Wild Card series. pic.twitter.com/1ecutsoJrt

item.content:encoded:
MLB | Velocidad pura: José Caballero llega a 34 estafadas con los Yankees
- martes 22 de septiembre de 2026 - 6:19 PM
Los Yankees de Nueva York se impusieron este martes 2-0 ante los Rays de Tampa Bay en el primer encuentro de una doble cartelera disputada en el Yankee Stadium, un duelo que tuvo al pelotero panameño José ‘Chema’ Caballero como uno de los protagonistas de la jornada al desplegar toda su velocidad y picardía en el terreno de juego.
Caballero, quien alineó como titular y se desempeñó en la tercera base, terminó el compromiso de 3-1 con un sencillo y dos bases robadas que mantuvieron bajo presión constante a la batería rival conformada por Nick Martínez y Liam Hicks. En la quinta entrada, el infielder istmeño sorprendió a la defensa con un toque suave que se convirtió en un valioso infield hit, para luego encadenar las estafadas de segunda y tercera base.
Con esta actuación ofensiva, el santeño elevó su total de la campaña a 34 bases robadas en 132 partidos, ubicándose de manera firme en la octava posición entre los máximos estafadores de todas las Grandes Ligas. Su línea ofensiva en lo que va de la temporada se mantiene en .236 de promedio, con 14 cuadrangulares, 51 carreras impulsadas y un OPS de .666.
El triunfo de los ‘Mulos de Manhattan’ también estuvo sustentado en una joya de pitcheo del zurdo Carlos Rodón, quien laboró de manera dominante durante ocho entradas sin permitir anotaciones, tolerando apenas tres imparables y recetando ocho ponches. Con esta labor, Rodón alcanzó su victoria número 100 en las Grandes Ligas y llegó a la cifra de 1,500 ponches en su carrera, en un partido que se completó en apenas dos horas y dos minutos.
La única diferencia en la pizarra llegó en la parte baja del cuarto episodio, cuando Cody Bellinger sacudió un cuadrangular de dos carreras ante los envíos de Nick Martínez para colocar el 2-0 definitivo. En la novena entrada, David Bednar se encargó de cerrar el candado para apuntarse su salvamento número 35 de la temporada, recortando la diferencia a cinco juegos en la lucha por la cima del Este de la Liga Americana.

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] Clarke Schmidt's return makes Yankees' October rotation a mess
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson

item.content:encoded:
The Yankees activated Clarke Schmidt from the 60-day injured list on Sept. 16. On paper, that should read like uncomplicated good news. In late September, it really is another decision sitting on the manager’s desk.
Clarke Schmidt has logged just two-thirds of an inning in 2026. He is active, but he has not had the time to rebuild a normal starter’s workload while Carlos Rodon, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Cam Schlittler are already taking up the big innings.
Add Will Warren to that conversation and the Yankees have more options than clean answers. A talented pitcher returning late is useful. It can also make the October board much harder to read.
The Yankees cannot let sentiment choose the role
Schmidt earned real trust before the injury, which makes this harder than it would be for a fringe arm. He is not someone the Yankees should stash in the background and forget about.
But a postseason roster does not care about last spring or last year. It cares about who can get through a difficult inning right now. The Yankees need to decide whether Schmidt can help as a short reliever, a piggyback option or simply depth behind their first group of starters.
The answer does not have to be permanent this week. It does need to be honest. Trying to force a long starter’s buildup into the final days of the season would create a problem the Yankees do not need.
October will reward the Yankees for getting practical
Schmidt returning gives the Yankees an extra good pitcher. That matters. The club should enjoy having more pitching than most teams can claim this late in the year.
Still, the safest route is probably the simplest one: use him in the role his current workload supports, then see if the games demand more. The Yankees have enough established starters. What they need from Schmidt is clarity, not a rushed label.
More about:New York Yankees

item.dc:creator: CBS New York Team
item.description: Carlos Rodón allowed three hits in eight sharp innings and the New York Yankees prevented the Tampa Bay Rays from clinching the AL East title with a 2-0 victory in the opener of a day-night doubleheader on Tuesday. The Yankees (90-66) moved six games ahead of the Red Sox for the AL's top wild-card spot. Tampa Bay (95-61) has a magic number of two to clinch the AL East for the fifth time in team history and first since 2021. Cody Bellinger hit a two-run homer in the fourth inning off Tampa Bay st
item.content:encoded:
Carlos Rodón allowed three hits in eight sharp innings and the New York Yankees prevented the Tampa Bay Rays from clinching the AL East title with a 2-0 victory in the opener of a day-night doubleheader on Tuesday.
The Yankees (90-66) moved six games ahead of the Red Sox for the AL's top wild-card spot. Tampa Bay (95-61) has a magic number of two to clinch the AL East for the fifth time in team history and first since 2021.
Cody Bellinger hit a two-run homer in the fourth inning off Tampa Bay starter Nick Martinez (15-5) and also started a key double play to end the sixth by throwing out Victor Mesa Jr. at first.
Rodón (7-3) struck out eight and walked none while completing eight innings for the first time since July 11, 2025, against the Cubs. The left-hander, who recorded his 100th win, became the 18th active pitcher to reach 1,500 career strikeouts when he fanned Jonny DeLuca on a slider for the second out of the eighth.
Rodón also struck out AL MVP candidate Junior Caminero on a slider in the dirt in the seventh with a runner on after reaching 98 mph on the previous two pitches.
Rodón threw first-pitch strikes to 15 of 25 hitters and improved to 3-1 in seven starts since returning from left elbow inflammation last month.
Following a double by Ben Rice off Martinez in the fourth, Bellinger lifted the next pitch into the right field seats for a 2-0 lead.
After a single by Mesa started the sixth, Richie Palacios lifted a fly ball to Bellinger. Bellinger made the catch and a strong one-hop throw to first baseman Luis García Jr. to easily complete the double play and get his eighth outfield assist this year.
Martinez allowed two runs and five hits in six innings. The right-hander struck out seven and lost for the first time since July 9.
David Bednar retired Yandy Díaz for his 35th save in 39 chances and finish New York's 15th shutout in 2 hours, 2 minutes - the Yankees' fastest game this season.
Up next
Tampa Bay RHP Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72 ERA) opposes New York LHP Max Fried (5-4, 2.63) in the second game.

item.title: [yardbarker.com] Carlos Rodon reaches multiple career milestones in victory over Rays
item.dc:creator: Bill Ladson

item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK — It’s safe to say New York Yankees left-hander Carlos Rodón is ready for the postseason. He pitched his best game of the season in a 2-0 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday afternoon.
Rodón pitched a season-high eight innings, allowed three hits and struck out eight batters. It was a quick game, which lasted two hours and two minutes.
“He was awesome,” Yankees manager Aaron Boone told reporters about Rodón. “His strike throwing was great. The fastball was in a really good place, a really good profile in the heater, too. The secondary (pitches) were good — the slider and changeup. … It was a really solid quick win.”
Rodón also reached a couple of milestones along the way, striking out his 1,500th batter in the seventh and winning his 100th game of his career. Rodón said when he started his big-league career with the Chicago White Sox on April 21, 2015 against the then-Cleveland Indians, he wasn’t looking into the future thinking that he was going to win a lot of games.
“At 22 (years old), it was a cold night in Chicago,” Rodón recalled to reporters. “I ran out to the mound and never saw three decks in a stadium before. So I was trying to keep my heart in my chest. The crystal ball wasn’t looking this far into the future.”
Rodón wasn’t nervous against the Rays, however. He had 18 swings and misses, and his fastball went as high as 97.5. For his 1,500th strikeout, Rodón struck out Jonny DeLuca on a 86.3 mph slider.
“During the moment, I didn’t know what was going on. I go, people are clapping. Cool. Fifteen hundred is nice. Hopefully, I can keep going,” Rodón said.
Rodón most likely started his last game of the season, although Boone hasn’t ruled out Rodón throwing on Sunday against the Orioles. The Yankees will go into the postseason without their best player, Aaron Judge. But Rodón is confident that the team will go far. He based it on what he saw in Tuesday’s game.
Cody Bellinger was clutch with a two-run homer in the fourth frame and was able to double off Victor Mesa Jr. at first base after Richie Palacio flew out to Bellinger in left field two-innings later.
“The bullpen is deep. The starters are really good. I have a lot of confidence in this club,” Rodón said.
All quotations obtained firsthand unless otherwise noted.

item.title: [pinstripealley.com] Yankees win first game of doubleheader behind Carlos Rodón’s milestone performance
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: The chances are now paper thin after a series loss in Arizona, but if the Yankees are to have any shot of chasing down the Rays in the final week of the season, they absolutely must sweep this four-game series. That required a dominant performance from Carlos Rodón facing one of the AL’s best starters in Nick Martinez. They certainly got that, Rodón running rampant for eight scoreless innings, achieving both the 1,500th strikeout and 100th win of his career as the Yankees took the first game of
item.content:encoded:
The chances are now paper thin after a series loss in Arizona, but if the Yankees are to have any shot of chasing down the Rays in the final week of the season, they absolutely must sweep this four-game series. That required a dominant performance from Carlos Rodón facing one of the AL’s best starters in Nick Martinez. They certainly got that, Rodón running rampant for eight scoreless innings, achieving both the 1,500th strikeout and 100th win of his career as the Yankees took the first game of the day’s doubleheader, 2-0.
Rodón burst out of the gate like he had a point to prove, whiffing the first two batters of the game Yandy Díaz and Jonathan Aranda on a pair of filthy sliders. Cam Schlittler and Max Fried are likely locks for the postseason rotation, meaning if the Yankees elect to stick with a three-man unit, that final spot comes down to Rodón and Gerrit Cole. Aaron Boone has affirmed his commitment to Cole as the Game One starter in a prospective Wild Card Series. This seemingly leaves Rodón on the bubble, which might explain the extra edge he was pitching with this afternoon.
His teammates didn’t do themselves any favors early, burning both ABS challenges in the first inning. I expect the Yankees to tighten the strings on who gets to challenge and in what situation come the playoffs as you cannot deprive yourself of such a vital tool with eight innings still to play.
Martinez entered this game with the lowest walk rate of any qualified starter and among the league’s best at limiting hard contact. He was true to form going the first turn through the order without allowing a base runner. He was helped by the collectively poor approach from the lineup, with four out of the nine batters including the side in the third striking out against a pitcher with the lowest strikeout rate among qualified starters.
That started to change the second turn through the order, the Yankees finally starting to do some damage against the high volume of pitches Martinez was throwing over the heart of the plate, starting with a Ben Rice double into the corner in right to lead off the fourth. The very next pitch Martinez threw rocketed out of the yard, Cody Bellinger blasting a first pitch sinker into the seats in right for a two-run homer — his fifth homer in the last 12 games.
George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones singled with two outs to put runners on the corners. Jones then stole second unopposed, but Anthony Volpe struck out swinging to strand the pair in scoring position. They kept up the pressure in the fifth, José Caballero reaching on a bunt single against his former team and then stealing second and third followed by a Rice walk to put runners on the corners with one out. However, Bellinger popped out and Heliot Ramos flew out as they stranded a pair in consecutive frames.
Rodón settled into an impressive groove after a Chandler Simpson single in the second, retiring the next ten batters in order until Victor Mesa Jr. led off the sixth with a single. After Rodón whiffed Jorge Mateo on a slider for his sixth strikeout, he got Richie Palacios to line out to left. Mesa was running on the play and momentarily forget he had to sprint back to first, allowing Bellinger to throw an absolute seed to Luis García Jr., who applid the tag for the inning-ending double play.
With Rodón’s pitch count standing at just 89 after seven, Boone decided to go batter-to-batter in the eighth. However, Rodón ensured his manager had no choice to make, completing the eighth inning on just seven pitches, including the 1,500th strikeout of his career. It’s tied for his longest start as a Yankee, matching the eight innings he pitched against the Cubs on July 11, 2025.
Rodón entered this start as perhaps the Yankees’ most in-form pitcher behind Schlittler. Including today, in his last eight starts, Rodón has a 1.67 ERA while holding batters to a measly .134 batting average against. He had all his pitches working today, but this really felt like a throwback to his peak years with Chicago and San Francisco. He got whiffs in bunches on the four-seamer above the zone and slider below it. In likely his penultimate start of the regular season, Rodón dominated for eight scoreless innings, allowing three hits and no walks while striking out eight to lower his ERA to 2.67 on the year.
The Yankees didn’t manage another base runner in the final three innings, but Rodón made sure that it wouldn’t come back to haunt them. David Bednar pitched a one-two-three ninth to secure his 35th save of the season. The gap to the Rays now stands at five games as the Yankees become the second team in the AL to 90 wins. At worst, they have clinched the four seed in the AL, guaranteeing home field advantage in a prospective AL Wild Card Series.
The Yankees have a few hours’ rest before taking the field again tonight. Max Fried starts the night game of the doubleheader against Drew Rasmussen. First pitch is scheduled for 7:05 pm ET with the broadcast remaining on YES, so stick around!

Rodón allowed only three hits, all singles, while striking out eight over eight scoreless innings. It was his first eight-inning performance since July 11, 2025. The left-hander retired 19 straight batters at one point, with two double plays helping preserve the perfect stretch. Jose Caballero started
item.content:encoded:
Carlos Rodón delivered his best starts of the season Tuesday afternoon, leading the New York Yankees to a 2-0 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays in the first game of a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.
Rodón allowed only three hits, all singles, while striking out eight over eight scoreless innings. It was his first eight-inning performance since July 11, 2025.
The left-hander retired 19 straight batters at one point, with two double plays helping preserve the perfect stretch. Jose Caballero started a 5-4-3 double play in the second inning, while Cody Bellinger caught a line drive in the third before throwing to first base, where Luis García Jr. tagged Victor Mesa Jr. trying to return to the bag.
Rodón also reached a career milestone in the eighth inning when he recorded his 1,500th strikeout. His season earned-run average dropped to 2.67, while he has posted a 1.42 earned-run average in four September starts.
New York’s offense struggled to generate much against Tampa Bay starter Nick Martinez, who retired the Yankees in order the first time through the lineup.
That changed in the fourth inning. Ben Rice opened the frame with a double before Bellinger followed with a two-run home run to right field, giving New York its only runs of the game.
George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones followed with consecutive two-out singles, but Anthony Volpe struck out to end the inning.
David Bednar closed the game with a scoreless ninth for his 35th save.
The victory moved New York to within five games of Tampa Bay in the American League East.
The teams meet again Tuesday at 7:05 p.m. Max Fried starts for New York against Drew Rasmussen.

item.title: [roundtable.io] Yankees' Carlos Rodon Could Shockingly Take Gerrit Cole's Job
item.dc:creator: Matthew Schmidt
item.description: New York Yankees pitcher Carlos Rodon is making quite a case for himself. The general consensus is that the Yankees' No. 2 and 3 starters will be some combination of Gerrit Cole and Max Fried, although Cole's recent struggles have now put a spotlight on the evolving situation. Carlos Rodon then intensified it with his performance on Tuesday afternoon. In the opener of New York's four-game series against the Tampa Bay Rays, Rodon tossed eight scoreless innings, registering nine strikeouts while a
item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees pitcher Carlos Rodon is making quite a case for himself.
The general consensus is that the Yankees' No. 2 and 3 starters will be some combination of Gerrit Cole and Max Fried, although Cole's recent struggles have now put a spotlight on the evolving situation.
Carlos Rodon then intensified it with his performance on Tuesday afternoon.
In the opener of New York's four-game series against the Tampa Bay Rays, Rodon tossed eight scoreless innings, registering nine strikeouts while allowing just three hits. He also didn't issue a single walk.
Quietly, Rodon has been enjoying a tremendous season, perhaps his best as a Yankee.
Yes, Rodon's 2026 campaign has been abbreviated, as he began the year on the shelf due to offseason elbow surgery and then missed some more time as a result of an elbow issue midway through the year, but in the 16 games he has pitched, Rodon owns a 2.67 ERA and 1.06 WHIP while averaging 9.7 strikeouts per nine innings.
What's more, Rodon has surrendered just two runs or less in each of his last eight starts, and he has allowed one run or less in six of them.
So has Rodon now entered the conversation as a potential No. 2 or 3 starter in the Yankees' postseason rotation? And could Cole get the boot?
Cole pitched considerably better in his last outing, giving up just two runs in six innings. However, his swing-and-miss stuff still wasn't there, and it's hard to ignore just how home-run prone he has been over the last month.
Chances are, Boone will give Cole the nod based on reputation and seniority alone, but let's say the 36-year-old has another middling start this week. Then what?
At that point, Boone would have to seriously consider giving Rodon the nod. The left-hander has flown under the radar in recent weeks, but he has truly been outstanding.
It sounds unheard of to remove Cole from the top three of the Yankees' playoff rotation. But results matter, and Cole has not produced a whole lot of positive ones recently.
We'll see if Boone ultimately makes what would be a surprising decision for the postseason.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees utility player Jose Caballero will get the start today at third base in the first game of a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Caballero (age 30) is a former Tampa Bay Ray who was traded to the Yankees at last year's MLB trade deadline. Caballero is hitting a .236 batting average with 14 home runs, 51 RBIs, 32 stolen bases, and a .665 OPS.
Ryan McMahon Yankees Dilemma
This is an interesting development, considering third baseman and left-handed hitter Ryan McMahon has been struggling significantly lately, both offensively and defensively.
This season, McMahon is hitting .208 with 10 home runs, 35 RBIs, and a .618 OPS. McMahon's throws from third base this year have been concerning at times as well. Caballero is an above-average defender and could provide more value offensively than McMahon is right now, so it makes sense why the Yankees are trying Caballero at third base in game one of the doubleheader today against Tampa.
Yankees Getting Ready For Playoffs
With the playoffs (Wild Card) just a week away, with game one beginning Tuesday, September 29th, now is the time for the Yankees to not only rest some key players but also try guys at different positions as they figure out how the postseason roster will ultimately shake out.
The Yankees are also still waiting on the return of Jazz Chisholm Jr., which raises another question: what do the Yankees do when it comes to playing either Anthony Volpe or Jazz Chisholm Jr. at second base, and what happens to the other?
Caballero has talked about trying to provide extra spark/energy to prove himself when playing for his former squad in Tampa. The Yankees will hope to see that effect from a different position in game one of the doubleheader and in this series as they look to wrap up the regular season on a positive note. In contrast, Tampa is looking for a win to clinch the AL East Division, with the winner in a likely wild-card race between the Yankees and Red Sox then going on to face Tampa Bay.
But how Caballero fares today at third base could offer a glimpse into the Yankees' postseason strategy as they prepare for the Wild Card round, which will be no easy task after navigating the AL East. It will also be interesting to see how much this move affects Ryan McMahon's playing time for the rest of the regular season and then the postseason, unless they view it as rest for McMahon.
This article was originally published on HEAVY

item.content:encoded:
Redacción Deportes, 22 sep (EFE)-. Los Yankees de Nueva York afrontarán previsiblemente una eventual Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana ante los Medias Rojas de Boston sin su capitán, Aaron Judge, quien sufre una distensión de "grado moderado" en la pantorrilla derecha y tiene comprometida su presencia en el inicio de la postemporada.
El manager Aaron Boone confirmó este martes que el equipo trabaja con el escenario de no contar con Judge, aunque dejó abierta la posibilidad de acelerar su recuperación si la situación lo requiere.
PUBLICIDAD
"Estamos planeando que no sea parte de eso", dijo Boone este martes. "Pero también estamos en una época del año en la que ... obviamente lo forzaríamos un poco si eso estuviera en juego. Pero falta una semana para eso. No lo espero, pero tampoco lo descarto".
Judge fue colocado el sábado en la lista de lesionados de 10 días, con efecto retroactivo al 17 de septiembre, después de sufrir la distensión durante la serie de la semana pasada contra los Mellizos de Minnesota.
El toletero recibió el lunes una inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas y tendrá actividad limitada durante los próximos días.
"El par de días siguientes no habrá mucho: nada de correr, saltar, cosas así", indicó Boone.
Judge explicó que la lesión afecta al músculo sóleo de la pantorrilla derecha, una zona que considera especialmente importante para correr y batear.
"He lidiado con distensiones antes y de alguna manera he jugado con ellas, pero esta fue en un lugar diferente donde lo hizo un poco más difícil", comentó Judge.
Una distensión de grado 2 en la pantorrilla suele requerir entre tres y seis semanas de recuperación, un plazo que complica su presencia en el comienzo de los playoffs.
"Si él es capaz de jugar, entonces le daremos esa oportunidad", señaló Boone.
Judge, que ya se perdió buena parte del verano por una fractura en la costilla derecha, apenas disputó siete partidos desde su regreso en septiembre. En 66 encuentros esta campaña bateó .241/.360/.511, con 18 jonrones y 41 carreras impulsadas
Los Yankees ya aseguraron su boleto a los playoffs, pero una victoria de los Rays de Tampa Bay en cualquiera de los encuentros de la doble cartelera de este martes les permitiría conquistar el Este de la Liga Americana y el primer sembrado de la liga, lo que enviaría a Nueva York a disputar la Serie del Comodín.EFE
PUBLICIDAD

item.title: [La Prensa Panamá] José Caballero llegó a 34 bases robadas en la victoria de los Yankees
item.dc:creator: Humberto Cornejo
item.description: José Caballero tuvo una buena actuación en la victoria de los Yankees de Nueva York 2-0 sobre los Rays de Tampa Bay, en el primer juego de una doble jornada disputada en el Yankee Stadium, al conectar un imparable y robarse dos bases. El panameño terminó el encuentro de 2-1, con un sencillo y dos bases estafadas, en una actuación clave dentro del triunfo neoyorquino. Caballero swipes third on a walk and he's now at 34 steals on the year! pic.twitter.com/wNUV5tAwkR — Talkin' Yanks (@TalkinYanks)
item.content:encoded:
José Caballero tuvo una buena actuación en la victoria de los Yankees de Nueva York 2-0 sobre los Rays de Tampa Bay, en el primer juego de una doble jornada disputada en el Yankee Stadium, al conectar un imparable y robarse dos bases.
El panameño terminó el encuentro de 2-1, con un sencillo y dos bases estafadas, en una actuación clave dentro del triunfo neoyorquino.
Caballero swipes third on a walk and he's now at 34 steals on the year! pic.twitter.com/wNUV5tAwkR
— Talkin' Yanks (@TalkinYanks) September 22, 2026
Caballero conectó un toque suave en la quinta entrada que terminó en infield hit, y desde allí aprovechó su velocidad para robarse la segunda y la tercera base, generando presión constante sobre la defensa rival. En este compromiso también se desempeñó en la tercera base.
Con esta actuación, el santeño dejó su línea ofensiva en .236 de promedio, con 14 jonrones y 51 carreras impulsadas, además de 34 bases robadas en 132 partidos.
Rodón domina desde la lomita
El triunfo de los Yankees también tuvo como figura al lanzador Carlos Rodón, quien trabajó de manera dominante durante ocho entradas sin permitir carreras.
Rodón permitió apenas tres imparables, no otorgó boletos y enfrentó el mínimo de bateadores durante gran parte del encuentro, además de recetar ponches en momentos clave para encaminar la victoria.
El zurdo alcanzó su victoria número 100 en Grandes Ligas y llegó a 1,500 ponches en su carrera tras retirar a Jonny DeLuca en la octava entrada.
CABALLERO IS FLYING! José Caballero swipes third after drawing a walk, giving him 34 stolen bases on the season! He’s now just 90 feet away from home as the Yankees look to add to their lead. pic.twitter.com/J2qig69isi
— Concrete City Sports (@concretecityccs) September 22, 2026
La ofensiva de los Yankees fue respaldada por un cuadrangular de dos carreras de Cody Bellinger, quien conectó su jonrón número 17 de la temporada en el cuarto episodio para sellar el 2-0 definitivo.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees hold off Rays' celebration with win in doubleheader opener
(Photo credit: Brad Penner)
Cody Bellinger hit a two-run home run in the fourth inning as the host New York Yankees recorded a 2-0 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays in the opener of a day-night doubleheader on Tuesday.
With the victory, the Yankees (90-66) prevented the Rays (95-61) from clinching the AL East and moved six games ahead of the Boston Red Sox for the American League's top wild-card spot.
Tampa Bay still has a magic number of two to clinch the fifth divisional title in team history and first since 2021.
New York's Carlos Rodon (7-3) scattered three singles over eight innings as the Yankees finished off the victory in a brisk 2 hours, 2 minutes. Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (15-5) allowed two runs on five hits over six innings with seven strikeouts to take his first loss since July 9.
Rodon allowed singles to Chandler Simpson in the second, Victor Mesa Jr. in the sixth and Jonathan Aranda in the seventh. The left-hander struck out eight in his 100th career win and longest outing since he went eight innings against the Chicago Cubs on July 11, 2025.
Rodon also reached 1,500 strikeouts when he set down Jonny DeLuca on a slider in the eighth.
Martinez retired the first nine Yankees hitters of the game before Ben Rice laced a double to right field to lead off the fourth inning and Bellinger hammered the next pitch to the right-field seats for a 2-0 lead.
It was Bellinger's 17th home run and sixth in his past 26 games.
Bellinger also started a key double play from left field to end the sixth. After Mesa opened the inning with a single, Richie Palacios lofted a fly ball to left with Bellinger making the catch then firing a one-hop throw to first baseman Luis Garcia Jr. to complete the double play.
It was Bellinger's eighth outfield assist of the season.
David Bednar finished New York's 15th shutout by retiring Yandy Diaz for his 35th save.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [fansided.com] Projecting the Yankees Wild Card series lineup after brutal Aaron Judge's injury update
item.dc:creator: Zachary Rotman

A September return following a three-month stint on the IL gave Judge enough time to find his timing before the postseason. item.content:encoded:
It felt like Aaron Judge was returning at the perfect time. A September return following a three-month stint on the IL gave Judge enough time to find his timing before the postseason. Unfortunately, Judge suffered another injury before the playoffs even began, hurting his calf in a game against the Minnesota Twins. The New York Yankees hoped it'd be minor, but it was serious enough for the team to place its captain on the Injured List. Now, it sounds as if a return for the Yankees' first postseason series is a long shot at best.
A "moderate grade" calf strain is serious enough for Yankees manager Aaron Boone to proceed as if his best player won't be active at all for the Wild Card series. That is an insanely difficult blow for a Yankees team that, with Judge, is as good as any in a weak American League. For the Yankees to advance to the ALDS and potentially get their captain back, they'll need to rely on this projected lineup below.
What the Yankees lineup could look like without Aaron Judge
Judge is an instrumental piece in the Yankees' lineup for a couple of reasons. First, he's the best hitter in the sport when healthy. That obviously matters. Second, Judge is one of the few right-handed bats on this roster. He provides much-needed balance that, without Judge, the Yankees lack.
| Position | Player |
|---|---|
| Ben Rice | DH |
| Cody Bellinger | LF |
| Heliot Ramos | RF |
| Luis Garcia Jr. | 1B |
| Spencer Jones | CF |
| George Lombard Jr. | SS |
| Jazz Chisholm Jr. | 2B |
| Austin Wells | C |
| Jose Caballero | 3B |
This lineup still has some good pieces in it. Ben Rice has had a breakout year, Cody Bellinger is a well-rounded star, and trails only Yordan Alvarez and Pete Crow-Armstrong, the AL and NL MVP favorites, with a .532 slugging percentage. If Jazz Chisholm Jr. can return from the IL looking like the player he's capable of being, the Yankees can score runs.
The problem, though, is that six of the nine hitters in this lineup are left-handed, and most of them are much better against righties than lefties. The Yankees will use guys like Paul Goldschmidt and Amed Rosario against left-handed pitching, but having Heliot Ramos, who has a .672 OPS since being acquired by the Yankees at the deadline, in the No. 3 hole against righties isn't ideal. The Yankees don't have much of a choice with Judge out, though.
Ultimately, with Judge out, this is a team heavily reliant on lineup platoons. It'll be on Aaron Boone to try to push the right buttons in order to get this offense, which has been remarkably inconsistent without Judge, to score runs against (likely) a potent Boston Red Sox pitching staff.
Aaron Judge injury update: Can the Yankees expect their star to return?
What's most frustrating about the Judge injury update is that we have no idea what the injury is. The Yankees, for whatever reason, keep information regarding injuries, particularly to Judge, extremely close to the vest, making it difficult to know when or even if Judge will be back. All we know is that Judge is dealing with what Aaron Boone deems a "moderate" strain.
That doesn't sound good, especially for a player who has had trouble with the same right calf in the past. In the shortened 2020 season, Judge attempted to return from a calf strain in a couple of weeks, but wound up re-aggravating the injury, pushing his return back several weeks. Calf injuries and other soft-tissue ailments are not to be messed with, and can lead to a major setback if rushed through.
Plus, if the injury was minor, wouldn't the Yankees be quick to tell the world that? I'd love to say Judge is a lock to return at some point, but even if the Yankees were to advance to the ALDS, given how little we know and how tricky returns can be from calf injuries, it's probably wishful thinking to assume he'd be back right at the start of a potential ALDS, which is the last thign any New York fan wants to hear.

item.content:encoded:
As the New York Yankees gear up for a postseason run, they need as many hot bats as possible to make noise.
Fortunately for the Bronx Bombers, a few players are beginning to settle into a groove at the right time. In an even more encouraging development, one of those players heating up is George Lombard Jr., the team's youngest player and shortstop of the future.
The 21-year-old has hit three home runs over his past 12 games and recorded three multi-hit games over that stretch. Although Lombard is only 11-for-46 (.239 batting average) in this span, his plate appearances in general are improving, as he's chasing less and swinging more often at strikes.
Heading into the first game of Tuesday's doubleheader against the Tampa Bay Rays, Lombard swung at 29.2% of pitches outside the strike zone and 65.5% inside the zone this season. But in the last 11 games prior to the doubleheader, it improved to 25.3%, and he swung at 69.6% of strikes, both of which are noticeable improvements over his total season rates.
Swinging at better pitches to hit has allowed Lombard to do more damage, including a 424-foot bomb against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Sunday.
George Lombard Jr. is steadily adapting to MLB pitching
One of Lombard's strengths as a prospect was adaptability. He would get off to slow starts at each minor league level he played, but then made the necessary adjustments at the plate to hit his way up to the next level.
His rise through Triple-A was the most impressive. After hitting just .184 in his first 27 games with Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, Lombard slashed .358/.471/.679 with 20 extra-base hits and 22 walks against 29 strikeouts over his next 31 games before getting the call to The Show.
Yet for all the growing pains he's gone through in the major leagues, Lombard didn't look as overmatched as he did when starting at Triple-A. He's held his own against established arms and is continuing to improve, if his last couple of games are any indication.
Now, Lombard is already going to face his greatest challenge yet: playing the best teams with the best pitching in a high-stakes environment. But playing meaningful baseball games over the past month should prepare him well for this opportunity, as he's faced the Atlanta Braves, Houston Astros, Boston Red Sox, San Diego Padres, and Rays since being called up.
Based on the postseason bracket alignment, the Yankees need to beat the Red Sox and Rays to advance to the ALCS. Lombard played in three of four games against Boston and is now getting his first look at Tampa Bay. The upward trajectory of his at-bats, coupled with acclimating himself to future opponents, should serve Lombard well in these playoff series and give the Yankees' offense some much-needed production.
Joe Najarian is a writer for Yankees On SI, having previously covered the Yankees both for SI and additional sites since 2023. He also served as Deputy Editor for the Yankees, Mets and Orioles On SI sites, and additionally contributes to Athlon Sports and Men’s Journal covering Major League Baseball and other trending sports news. Joe is a graduate of Rutgers University in 2022, earning a bachelor’s degree in Journalism and Media Studies.

item.content:encoded:
A flurry of injury news came across for the battered and bruised Bronx Bombers on Tuesday at Yankee Stadium.
While the team is clearly compromised and will likely be missing their best player, Aaron Judge, when the playoffs start on Sept. 29, they will be getting their second baseman back with some time to get ready for the inevitable Wild Card Series vs. the Boston Red Sox.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. is expected to be activated between games on Tuesday as the Bombers begin their four-game set with the Tampa Bay Rays with a day-night doubleheader. Chisholm Jr. has been out since Sept. 8 with a right thumb sprain.
“He should be in a good spot and ready to go,” said manager Aaron Boone. “He’s been hitting now for several days and and throwing the last three or four days, so he should be ready to go.”
The 28-year-old is slashing .232/.312/.403 with 19 homers and 55 RBI in 134 games this season. The impending free agent is expected to resume duties as their starting second baseman, which likely doesn’t bode well for Anthony Volpe’s playing time.
“Obviously, Anthony’s done a good job,” said Boone. “But looking forward to getting Jazz back as well. So, Jazz, I plan on playing Jazz at second in the night game.”
Volpe has performed well since being recalled from Triple-A on Sept. 10, slashing .286/.324/.429 with a homer, seven RBI and four stolen bases. It remains to be seen how he will be utilized and if a platoon scenario between Volpe and Chisholm Jr. is on the table.
CLARKE GOOD
Clarke Schmidt appears to have avoided anything major after experiencing bicep soreness while warming up during Sunday’s loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks.
“Clark is gonna play catch [Tuesday]. He did have some testing and it looks like he’s in a pretty good spot.” Boone said. “But [he’s] gotta throw and see how he is, and then we’ll go from there. … He’s on the active roster for now, but he’s got to play catch and do all those things and see how available he is.”
Schmidt returned from Tommy John surgery on Sept. 16 against the Minnesota Twins. He is expected to play a crucial role out of the bullpen in whatever time the Yankees have in the postseason.
WEATHERS UPDATE
Ryan Weathers (left forearm flexor strain) will throw a side session between games on Tuesday. Weathers exited his start against the Toronto Blue Jays on Aug 22 after feeling discomfort and has not appeared in a game since.
If the southpaw is to return in the postseason, it will very likely be out of the bullpen.

item.title: [New York Daily News] Carlos Rodón dominates as Yankees beat Rays in first game of doubleheader, keep AL East dreams alive
item.dc:creator: Peter Sblendorio
item.description: Given the depth of the Yankees’ rotation, there’s a strong possibility — perhaps even a likelihood — that Carlos Rodón won’t be asked to start a game in the best-of-three Wild Card round of the playoffs.T But Rodón looked every bit of an ace in Tuesday afternoon’s 2-0 win over the Tampa Bay Rays to kick off a doubleheader in the Bronx — a victory that kept the Yankees’ dreams of a division crown alive for at least a little while longer. item.content:encoded:
Given the depth of the Yankees’ rotation, there’s a strong possibility — perhaps even a likelihood — that Carlos Rodón won’t be asked to start a game in the best-of-three Wild Card round of the playoffs.T
But Rodón looked every bit of an ace in Tuesday afternoon’s 2-0 win over the Tampa Bay Rays to kick off a doubleheader in the Bronx — a victory that kept the Yankees’ dreams of a division crown alive for at least a little while longer.
Rodón hurled a season-high eight innings, striking out eight while limiting the Rays to three hits (all singles) without issuing a walk.
An eighth-inning strikeout of Jonny DeLuca was the 1,500th of Rodón’s 12-year career. Two pitches later, Rodón induced a soft groundout by Victor Mesa Jr. to end the inning, then walked off the mound to a standing ovation.
With the win — the 100th of his career — Rodón improved to 7-3 with a 2.67 ERA. A two-run home run by Cody Bellinger against Nick Martinez in the fourth inning provided all the run support Rodón would need.
It was the 26th start in a row in which Rodón limited an opponent to three runs or fewer, extending a franchise record.
Offseason elbow surgery delayed Rodón’s season debut until May 10, and he missed more than a month over the summer due to left elbow inflammation.
That’s limited Rodón to only 16 starts this season, and before Tuesday, he had not pitched more than 6.1 innings in any of them.
But Rodón has been consistently sharp over his 84.1 innings, and he’s pitching better than ever as the postseason approaches.
Whether Rodón actually gets to make a playoff start, however, may depend on whether the Yankees advance to the ALDS.
By winning game one of Tuesday’s doubleheader, the Yankees cut their deficit in the AL East to five games with six to play. But they began the day knowing they would need to sweep the division-leading Rays in this week’s four-game series to keep that goal alive.
Cam Schlittler is guaranteed to start a Wild Card game for the Yankees, while manager Aaron Boone said last week that he expects Gerrit Cole to start one, too.
That would leave one more game for either Rodón or Max Fried, who entered Tuesday’s nightcap with a 5-4 record and a 2.63 ERA.
In six playoff starts with the Yankees, Rodón is 1-2 with a 6.92 ERA.

item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays will get two chances to clinch their first American League East title since 2021 when they visit the New York Yankees for a day/night doubleheader on Tuesday.
With a magic number of two over the Yankees, the Rays can seal their fate in the afternoon opener.
Tampa Bay (95-60) has won six of the nine games against New York and owns a six-game lead on the Yankees. New York (89-66) has a magic number of two for clinching the AL's top wild-card spot over the Boston Red Sox.
The Rays, who are seeking their fifth division title, have led the AL East every day since June 27.
Following a 2-7 run last month, Tampa Bay is 19-7 since Aug. 23 and just went 8-1 on a homestand against the Houston Astros, Athletics and Red Sox. It featured three walk-off wins and ended with Sunday's 5-1 win over Boston which saw Chandler Simpson and Jonny DeLuca drive in two runs apiece.
"We knew what we had to do," Tampa Bay pitcher Griffin Jax said. "We wanted to put ourselves in a good place going into New York, make it a little bit easier."
The Yankees play host to the Rays for the first time since Aaron Judge's game-ending two-run homer for a 2-0 victory May 24. Judge returned Sept. 8 after missing 84 games with a fractured rib, played seven games and returned to the injured list with a strained calf.
The Yankees are 48-41 in games Judge has not played and enter the upcoming series after losing two of three at Arizona, including an 8-4 loss Sunday. Rookies George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones hit two of New York's three home runs in the third inning, but Brent Headrick gave up a grand slam to Arizona's Nolan Arenado in the fifth.
"We're going to show up and try to win the games on Tuesday, and then we'll keep going from there," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "We've been through a lot as a team this year already, and we've answered the bell at the turns. We're looking forward to hopefully playing a good week of baseball and building some momentum going into the postseason."
Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94 ERA) will start the opener for Tampa Bay followed by Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72) in the second game. Martinez is 3-0 with a 2.43 ERA in his past five starts and 2-2 with a 4.30 ERA in 12 career appearances against the Yankees.
Since allowing six runs in 2 1/3 innings at home against the Yankees on July 9, Rasmussen is 8-0 with a 1.91 ERA in his past 11 starts. He is 4-2 with a 1.87 ERA in 10 career outings against the Yankees.
New York will start Carlos Rodon (6-3, 2.95) in the opener followed by Max Fried (5-4, 2.63).
Rodon is 2-1 with a 2.40 ERA in six starts since returning from the injured list Aug. 18 and is 3-3 with a 3.88 ERA in 10 career starts against the Rays
Fried is 1-0 with a 1.83 ERA in four starts since returning from the injured list Aug. 29 and allowed one run in seven innings last Tuesday at Minnesota. He is 5-0 with a 1.26 ERA in six career starts against Tampa Bay.

item.title: [MLB.com] Judge se perdería la Serie del Comodín por distensión “moderada” en la pantorrilla
item.dc:creator: Bryan Hoch
item.description: NUEVA YORK -- Aaron Judge tiene una distensión de “grado moderado” en la pantorrilla derecha y probablemente se pierda al menos el inicio de la postemporada de los Yankees, según el manager Aaron Boone, quien dijo que el club no planea tener a su capitán activo para una posible Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana contra los Medias Rojas. “Estamos planeando que no sea parte de eso”, dijo Boone el martes. “Pero también estamos en una época del año en la que... obviamente lo forzaríamos un poco
item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK -- Aaron Judge tiene una distensión de “grado moderado” en la pantorrilla derecha y probablemente se pierda al menos el inicio de la postemporada de los Yankees, según el manager Aaron Boone, quien dijo que el club no planea tener a su capitán activo para una posible Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana contra los Medias Rojas.
“Estamos planeando que no sea parte de eso”, dijo Boone el martes. “Pero también estamos en una época del año en la que... obviamente lo forzaríamos un poco si eso estuviera en juego. Pero falta una semana para eso. No lo espero, pero tampoco lo descarto”.
Los Yankees han asegurado un pase a la postemporada, pero los Rays pueden amarrar el título del Este de la Liga Americana y el sembrado Nro. 1 de la L.A. con una victoria en cualquiera de los choques de la doble cartelera del martes, lo que obligaría a Nueva York a disputar la Serie del Comodín.
Judge fue ingresado a la lista de lesionados de 10 días el sábado, retroactivo al 17 de septiembre.
Recibió una inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas en la pantorrilla derecha durante el día libre del lunes y tendrá actividades limitadas durante los próximos días.
“El par de días siguientes no habrá mucho: nada de correr, saltar, cosas así”, indicó Boone.
Durante la serie del club el fin de semana en Phoenix, Judge y Boone fueron vagos sobre la gravedad de la lesión, la cual Judge sufrió durante la serie de la semana pasada frente a los Mellizos.
Judge reveló que la distensión es en el músculo sóleo de su pantorrilla derecha, el cual dijo “es un poco más crucial al correr y batear”.
“He lidiado con distensiones antes y de alguna manera he jugado con ellas, pero esta fue en un lugar diferente donde lo hizo un poco más difícil”, comentó Judge.
Generalmente, una distensión de pantorrilla de Grado 2 toma de tres a seis semanas para recuperarse.
“Si él es capaz de jugar, entonces le daremos esa oportunidad”, señaló Boone.
Judge se perdió la mayor parte del verano con una fractura en la costilla derecha, que se cree sufrió el 26 de abril en Houston. Jugó con la lesión antes de ingresar a la lista de lesionados a principios de junio.
Activado en septiembre sin una asignación de rehabilitación en liga menor, Judge disputó sólo siete compromisos después de ser activado, bateando de 23-4 (.174) con un jonrón. En general, Judge bateó .241/.360/.511 con 18 bambinazos y 41 carreras impulsadas en 66 partidos esta campaña.
“Hemos jugado gran parte del año sin él, y en su mayor parte, hemos hecho un trabajo bastante bueno”, destacó Boone. “Obviamente, siempre quieres a tu mejor jugador disponible. Pero entendemos que tenemos un trabajo que hacer y una expectativa de ganar. Creo que esa expectativa no cambia, con o sin él”.
En otras actualizaciones de lesiones, Boone dijo que los Yankees tienen la intención de activar al infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr. entre los encuentros de la doble cartelera del martes.
El derecho Clarke Schmidt se sometió a estudios de imagen tras necesitar acortar su calentamiento el domingo en Phoenix debido a una molestia en su bíceps derecho.
“Por ahora está en el roster activo, pero tiene que soltar el brazo y hacer todas esas cosas para ver qué tan disponible está”, declaró Boone.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees Announce Paul Goldschmidt Decision Before Rays Doubleheader
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Vankin

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are coming off two straight losses in Arizona to the Diamondbacks, a setback that left them a full six games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League East pennant race.
But the Yankees still have a chance to win the division and with it, the top seed in the AL and a bye out of the Wild card playoff round.
The Yankees and Rays open a four-game, head-to-head series with the first game of a doubleheader Tuesday at Yankee Stadium. With a four-game sweep, the Yankees would take the season tiebreaker and need to win at least two of three against the Baltimore Orioles, while the Rays lose two of three to the Philadelphia Phillies to close out the regular season.
Before Game One of the twin bill, the Yankees announced a decision on how they will utilize veteran first basinal Paul Goldschmidt.
Goldschmidt is out of the New York Yankees lineup for a third straight game, sidelined again by a stark platoon split against right-handed pitching.
The pattern has held all September, and it likely has fans wondering about how much longer the 39-year-old holds even a part-time role with October two weeks away.
| NEW YORK YANKEES STARTING LINEUP (GAME 1) | | | | |
| SP: Carlos Rodón (LHP) • 6-3, 2.95 ERA | | | | |
| September 22, 2026 • Yankee Stadium, Bronx, NY • 1:05 PM ET • Rays at Yankees | | | | |
| # | Player | Pos | AVG | SLG |
| 1 | Ben Rice | DH | .261 | .528 |
| 2 | Cody Bellinger | LF | .270 | .435 |
| 3 | Heliot Ramos | RF | .241 | .409 |
| 4 | Luis García Jr. | 1B | .281 | .532 |
| 5 | George Lombard Jr. | SS | .235 | .386 |
| 6 | Spencer Jones | CF | .248 | .442 |
| 7 | Anthony Volpe | 2B | .248 | .340 |
| 8 | Alí Sánchez | C | .250 | .316 |
| 9 | José Caballero | 3B | .236 | .373 |
| Lineups confirmed. Season stats shown (AVG / SLG). Umpire: Sean Barber • Weather: 63°, Wind 13 mph • O/U: 7 Runs • Line: TB +112 / NYY -135. | | | | |
Boone's Platoon Explains Goldschmidt Sit
Aaron Boone's lineup card for Tuesday's series opener against Tampa Bay leaves Goldschmidt out again, extending a run that traces back to Saturday. He started Friday against left-hander Eduardo Rodriguez in Arizona and went 1-for-4 with a walk and two runs, then sat both weekend games against right-handers Brandon Pfaadt and Corbin Burnes. That's three benchings in the last three games against right-handed starters.
Why? Goldschmidt has produced an elite 1.006 OPS against lefties this season but an anemic a .572 mark versus right-handers, a gap wide enough that Boone starts Ben Rice at DH and Luis García Jr. at first whenever a right-hander pitches. An Athletic report on the lineup moves after Aaron Judge's calf strain named Goldschmidt and Heliot Ramos as the bats Boone leans on against lefties, with García handling the right-handed side.
Nick Martinez, Tuesday's Tampa Bay starter, has largely dominated Goldschmidt in his career. The former National League MVP is 2-for-10 with four walks and two strikeouts against Martinez, and he is 0-for-13 with four strikeouts in his last three meetings with the right-hander since 2024. Martinez enters at 15-4 with a 2.94 ERA this year, and beat the Yankees in the Bronx in May, giving Boone both the season splits and the head-to-head history pointing toward a Goldschmidt benching.
Tuesday's day-night doubleheader against two more right-handed Rays starters gives Boone an easy excuse to sit the 39-year-old.
| TAMPA BAY RAYS STARTING LINEUP (GAME 1) | | | | |
| SP: Nick Martinez (RHP) • 15-4, 2.94 ERA | | | | |
| September 22, 2026 • Yankee Stadium, Bronx, NY • 1:05 PM ET • Rays at Yankees | | | | |
| # | Player | Pos | AVG | SLG |
| 1 | Yandy Díaz | DH | .292 | .449 |
| 2 | Jonathan Aranda | 1B | .277 | .440 |
| 3 | Junior Caminero | 3B | .277 | .529 |
| 4 | Liam Hicks | C | .288 | .440 |
| 5 | Chandler Simpson | LF | .309 | .360 |
| 6 | Jonny DeLuca | CF | .259 | .410 |
| 7 | Victor Mesa Jr. | RF | .251 | .502 |
| 8 | Ben Williamson | SS | .244 | .328 |
| 9 | Richie Palacios | 2B | .234 | .377 |
| Lineups confirmed. Season stats shown (AVG / SLG). Umpire: Sean Barber • Weather: 63°, Wind 13 mph • O/U: 7 Runs • Line: TB +112 / NYY -135. | | | | |
Goldschmidt's Future in New York
Goldschmidt turns free agent again this winter, and the Yankees have made no public commitment either way. A cheap return as a lefty-masher and clubhouse mentor remains plausible given Rice's grip on first base, and his credentials, a 2022 NL MVP award, seven All-Star selections, four Gold Gloves and five Silver Sluggers still makes him a name teams will inquire about this winter.
First base belongs to Rice, who has grown into an everyday role with 39 home runs and 95 RBI this season, pushing Goldschmidt into a complementary, short-side platoon job. That role fits the final stretch of a one-year, $4 million contract that can grow by $500,000 at each of four plate-appearance thresholds, according to Spotrac, a modest deal compared with the $12.5 million he earned in his first Yankees season a year earlier.
