item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.description: D-backs strive to make more 'magic' happen vs. Yankees (Photo credit: Matt Kartozian) Arizona manager Torey Lovullo said he felt 'a little bit of magic' in a 5-3 walk-off win over the New York Yankees on Saturday, the night the Diamondbacks celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series title. item.content:encoded:
D-backs strive to make more 'magic' happen vs. Yankees
(Photo credit: Matt Kartozian)
Arizona manager Torey Lovullo said he felt 'a little bit of magic' in a 5-3 walk-off win over the New York Yankees on Saturday, the night the Diamondbacks celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series title.
The Diamondbacks will take wins however they can get them as they continue an uphill fight for a National League wild-card berth in Sunday afternoon's finale of a three-game series vs. the Yankees in Phoenix.
New York's Will Warren (10-6, 3.89 ERA) will oppose Arizona's Corbin Burnes (0-0, 5.87) in a battle of right-handers.
'There was a ton of energy in the stadium,' said Lovullo, noting that most of the players from the 2001 team were on hand, 'so maybe there was a little bit of magic somewhere in these rafters that everybody picked up on.'
Pavin Smith's two-run, game-winning homer saved the Diamondbacks for a night, but work remains.
'We have to get inside a certain number,' said Lovullo, whose team will finish the regular season next week with a pair of three-game series at Colorado and San Diego. 'We know it, and this team is driving for something they feel they are able to do.'
Arizona (81-74) is five games behind the Chicago Cubs (86-69) and San Diego (86-69) and four behind Philadelphia (85-70) for the NL's three wild-card spots. Each team has seven games remaining.
The Yankees (89-65) fell five games behind first-place Tampa Bay (94-60) in the AL East. Those teams will meet in a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader on Tuesday and already have clinched a postseason berth.
'I have a ton of confidence in the guys we have rolling out there right now,' New York manager Aaron Boone said after Aaron Judge (calf strain) landed on the 10-day injured list Saturday.
Warren worked the Yankees' playoff clincher Monday at Minnesota, although he did not get a decision after giving up two runs (both unearned) in 5 2/3 innings of an 8-3 win. He struck out six and walked two.
Warren has been a workhorse on a staff that has faced injury issues. He will make his 29th start, second on the team behind Cam Schlittler (32).
'We've got a veteran core that's been here before, and we're looking to do big things,' Warren said of the upcoming postseason.
Warren has faced the Diamondbacks once in his career, giving up two runs on one hit -- a Corbin Carroll two-run homer -- in five innings of a no-decision on April 1, 2025.
Burnes will make his third start since being activated from the injured list Sept. 8 after a 15-month absence following Tommy John surgery. He gave up five runs in 4 2/3 innings but didn't figure into the decision in Monday's 8-7 victory over Miami, striking out four with no walks.
'It's all about cutter command,' Burnes said of his pet pitch, which he traditionally throws about 50% of the time. 'Just have to be more consistent with that,'
Burnes is 0-2 with a 1.93 ERA in four career starts against the Yankees. Paul Goldschmidt is 10-for-34 with a homer against the four-time All-Star and 2021 NL Cy Young Award winner.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Michael Fulmer News: Serves up walk-off homer Saturday
Fulmer (0-1) took the loss after allowing two runs on one hit and one walk while striking out one over one-third of an inning Saturday against the Diamondbacks.
Fulmer entered for the bottom of the ninth in a 3-3 game and opened the frame by walking Ildemaro Vargas. Even though he struck out Jordan Lawlar in the next at-bat, Fulmer would give up a walk-off two-run blast to pinch hitter Pavin Smith. This was the Yankees' 11th walk-off loss of the season, and it also ended Fulmer's streak of five consecutive scoreless relief appearances. The veteran right-hander owns a 3.09 ERA across 13 relief outings between the Angels and Yankees in 2026, but he has a 1.38 ERA in 10 appearances with the Bronx Bombers.

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] Austin Wells just made the Yankees think twice about his October role
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: Austin Wells has spent most of 2026 trying to climb out of a hole. His season line still carries the scars, but the past few weeks have looked a lot less bleak. Wells went 2-for-3 with a homer and a walk in Friday’s loss to Arizona. Since Sept. 1, he has three homers, nine walks and a .772 OPS in 15 games. The Yankees cannot pretend that is meaningless with October approaching. I do not buy the idea that three weeks erase a bad season. Wells has a .610 OPS overall, and any playoff decision has t
item.content:encoded:
Austin Wells has spent most of 2026 trying to climb out of a hole. His season line still carries the scars, but the past few weeks have looked a lot less bleak.
Wells went 2-for-3 with a homer and a walk in Friday’s loss to Arizona. Since Sept. 1, he has three homers, nine walks and a .772 OPS in 15 games. The Yankees cannot pretend that is meaningless with October approaching.
I do not buy the idea that three weeks erase a bad season. Wells has a .610 OPS overall, and any playoff decision has to account for the longer sample. But he is working counts, getting on base and putting a few mistakes in the seats again. He looks different from the hitter fans watched grind through much of the summer.
The Yankees have not solved catcher
The tempting move would be to call this a nice finish and keep the pecking order exactly where it was. That would miss the point. A club does not need Wells to become an All-Star in two weeks. It needs him to keep giving the lineup a real at-bat from a position that has been a drag far too often.
The catcher’s defense and handling of the staff will remain part of the equation. They should. Still, a second half that ends with better plate decisions and a little power makes the choice less automatic.
October should stay open for Wells
The Yankees do not have to hand Wells a postseason job today. They should keep running him out there while he is producing and see whether this run has another gear.
It is not a miracle comeback story. It is a late chance to turn a disappointing year into a harder decision, which beats entering October with no decision at all.
More about:New York Yankees

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Torey Lovullo has said the same phrase several times over the past seven years, even as fans and sometimes reporters rolled their eyes at the Arizona Diamondbacks manager’s optimism.
“Pavin Smith can hit,” Lovullo would say.
And on Saturday night, he finally did, injecting some life into the D-backs’ slim playoff hopes by smacking a game-ending, two-run homer in the ninth inning for a 5-3 win over the New York Yankees. Entering as a pinch-hitter, the left-hander ripped a cutter from Michael Fulmer over the right-field wall.
The D-backs pulled within four games of Philadelphia for the final NL wild card with seven games remaining.
“I’m never looking to be proven right,” Lovullo said. “I’m just trying to put players in the best position to be successful and when they have success I share it with them. But I do believe Pavin can hit.”
Smith has had an up-and-down career with the D-backs after being selected with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2017 amateur draft after a stellar three seasons in college at Virginia. He has a career batting average of .241 with 47 homers, but has been worth exactly 0.0 wins above replacement, according to baseball-reference.com.
The 30-year-old looked like he might finally be ready for his breakout season this spring, but he developed bone spurs in his elbow in March and needed surgery. That knocked him out of action for roughly two months.
He returned to the lineup on June 1, but looked lost at the plate. The low point came on July 9 when he was designated for assignment by the only organization he had ever known. At the time, he was hitting .141.
Smith cleared waivers, meaning 29 other teams didn’t think he was worth picking up. Then the D-backs sent him back to Triple-A Reno, where he slowly regained confidence in his swing.
Now he’s making big contributions at a critical stage of the season.
“It felt really good,” Smith said. “There were lots of times this year when I didn’t feel like I could ever hit again. I think that happens to a lot of people. Just didn’t have any timing coming back from the surgery.”
Smith’s homer was a crowd-pleaser at Chase Field, where a season-high 47,918 fans were in attendance for the franchise’s 25-year anniversary celebration of their 2001 World Series win over the Yankees.
Lovullo said their might have been a little magic in the air for the D-backs since so many franchise legends were in the building, including Luis Gonzalez, whose bloop single off Yankees closer and Hall of Famer Mariano Rivera in the ninth inning of Game 7 scored Jay Bell for a 3-2 win.
“Gonzo hit a walk-off about 25 years ago and to be able to do it on the (celebration) night is pretty cool,” Smith said. “It’s a full stadium. It was a playoff-like atmosphere. Every pitch felt like it mattered more and to pull it out in the end feels good.”

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees’ Cam Schlittler Joins Walter Johnson in Baseball History
item.dc:creator: Billy Heyen
item.description: Cam Schlittler didn't earn a win on Saturday night, because the New York Yankees' bullpen let the game get away from them in Arizona against the Diamondbacks. Schlittler did, as he has done so often this season, make some more baseball history. This history requires us to go back more than a century to a man named Walter Johnson. item.content:encoded:
Cam Schlittler didn't earn a win on Saturday night, because the New York Yankees' bullpen let the game get away from them in Arizona against the Diamondbacks.
Schlittler did, as he has done so often this season, make some more baseball history.
This history requires us to go back more than a century to a man named Walter Johnson.
Fans of baseball record books and history will know Johnson's name. He was known as the "Big Train," viewed by many as the first flamethrower that MLB ever had.
Johnson pitched for the Washington Senators, and he ranks second in the history of the sport in wins, behind just Cy Young.
He also, as one might expect, had some remarkable statistical feats during his day. And somehow, more than 100 years later, Schlittler has joined him on a couple lists.
Cam Schlittler and Walter Johnson
Schlittler's latest feat has to do with his ERA on the road, which has been finalized for the season because his last possible start will have to come at home in the week ahead.
The lanky righty has finished the year with a 1.16 ERA on the road.
The only player in the history of the American League to go lower than that is Johnson. In 1913, he had a 1.06 ERA on the road, according to New York Yankees Stats on X:
Cam Schlittler finishes the season with a 1.16 road ERA.
The only pitcher in American League history with a lower ERA on the road is Walter Johnson’s 1.06 in 1913 (min. 15 GS).
— New York Yankees Stats (@nyyankeesstats) September 20, 2026
Schlittler also is on a list for his entire body of work just behind Johnson. He's now got the third-most starts in a season in AL history in which he allowed no more than one earned run:
Most starts allowing 0-1 ER in a season, American League history (excluding openers)
27 Walter Johnson 1913
26 Walter Johnson 1914
24 Cam Schlittler 2026
— New York Yankees Stats (@nyyankeesstats) September 20, 2026
Baseball is such a cool sport historically, because all the information means that it's possible to realize that a pitcher in 2026 hasn't done something since a pitcher in 1913.
The game has obviously changed so much, but many of the numbers haven't, and it creates this great potential for comparison.
It also emphasizes just how special Schlittler has been this season. When you have to go back more than a century to find a peer, that's pretty incredible.
Cy Young Chatter
Schlittler is chasing the AL Cy Young, and a couple things have leaned in his favor this week.
For one, Dylan Cease had his worst outing of the season for the Toronto Blue Jays.
And as far as Cease is concerned, Toronto even has less of a chance to make the playoffs now, which lowers the overall vibes around his season relative to Schlittler.
It could still be close, but Schlittler is trying to put the finishing touches on his case for the award.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Yankees' Cam Schlittler Joins Walter Johnson in Baseball History appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Los Yankees incluyeron oficialmente a Aaron Judge en la lista de lesionados de 10 días este sábado, con efecto retroactivo desde el jueves, y han llamado a Max Schuemann. Judge no podrá volver antes del 27 de septiembre, el último día de la temporada regular, y se perderá la serie de cuatro partidos contra los Rays en el Yankee Stadium.
Eso no deja casi margen para una preparación normal antes de que empiece la Serie de Comodines de la Liga Americana el 29 de septiembre. Judge había vuelto el 8 de septiembre tras una ausencia de 99 días por una fractura por estrés en la primera costilla derecha. Antes de la lesión en la pantorrilla, había bateado 4 de 23, con un jonrón y 13 strikeouts.
El momento es especialmente malo porque Judge acababa de empezar a recuperar su swing. El jonrón de tres carreras que bateó el lunes en Minnesota fue el primero desde que volvió. Dos días después, notó una tensión en la parte inferior de la pierna derecha durante la primera entrada, siguió en el partido y no se retiró hasta que Heliot Ramos entró como bateador suplente por él en la sexta.
Una resonancia magnética realizada en Phoenix reveló la distensión. Judge dijo el sábado que se trata del sóleo, lo que describió como «algo más grave a la hora de correr y batear». No quiso dar detalles sobre la gravedad de la lesión, y Aaron Boone volvió a negarse a dar un plazo de recuperación.
Los Yankees ya saben lo que puede suponer su ausencia. Desde el 2 de junio hasta el 7 de septiembre, Nueva York ocupó el puesto 29 de las Grandes Ligas con un wRC+ de 90 y un promedio de bateo de 0,227, el 28 en wOBA y el 27 en OPS. El pitcheo fue lo que, en gran medida, mantuvo a flote a los Yankees.
La historia reciente de los Yankees hace que sea más difícil pasar por alto esta apuesta
Los partidos de rehabilitación no garantizan la buena forma física. Su valor radica en la repetición controlada, las pruebas de recuperación y la exposición al ritmo de juego antes de que llegue la intensidad de la postemporada.
La historia reciente de los Yankees nos invita a la cautela. Matt Carpenter volvió tras una fractura en el pie para la postemporada de 2022 y acabó con un 1 de 12 y nueve strikeouts. En 2019, Edwin Encarnación volvió tras una distensión en los oblicuos y bateó .056 en la ALCS, mientras que Gary Sánchez bateó .129 tras una lesión en la ingle en septiembre.
Esos ejemplos no predicen cómo le irá a Judge, pero sí muestran por qué es importante el momento. Si está listo el 27 de septiembre, los Yankees tendrían un partido de la temporada regular antes de los playoffs. Si no, su primer partido tras la baja podría ser bajo la presión de los playoffs y sin apenas preparación en condiciones reales.
Las decisiones del juez sobre quiénes volverán están ahora en el punto de mira
La segunda lesión hizo que el debate pasara de centrarse en la mala suerte a centrarse en las decisiones relacionadas con el regreso de Judge. Él dejó claro en agosto que quería saltarse la etapa de rehabilitación en las ligas menores, y los Yankees se lo permitieron.
El juez solo se había enfrentado a lanzamientos en directo una vez antes de su reincorporación. Cuando los Yankees le limitaron a seis entradas en su regreso el 8 de septiembre, dejó claro que no le gustaba nada esa restricción, aunque el plan se había discutido de antemano.
«Respeto a Booney, así que haré lo que él diga. Pero no me hace ninguna gracia», dijo Judge después de ese partido.
Ahora esa secuencia parece un poco rara. No demuestra que una asignación de rehabilitación hubiera evitado la lesión, y Boone rechaza esa conclusión. Pero saltarse los partidos de las ligas menores y luego negarse a seguir una carga de trabajo controlada ha avivado las dudas sobre la preparación.
El juez se mantiene firme a medida que se va acabando octubre
El propio Judge les dio a los Yankees una idea más clara de su lesión el sábado, pero no el plazo que necesitan.
El capitán dijo que la distensión en la pantorrilla derecha afecta al músculo sóleo y que volver para la postemporada es «sin duda el plan». Unas horas más tarde, Nueva York perdió 5-3 contra Arizona, quedando con un balance de 89-65 y a cinco partidos de Tampa Bay, cuando quedan ocho partidos por disputar.
«Me gustaría volver para la fase final. Ese es, sin duda, el plan. La verdad es que no te puedo dar ninguna respuesta sobre plazos ni nada por el estilo», dijo Judge tras el partido.
Eso prácticamente lo dejó fuera de esta temporada regular.
Judge sigue sin cuestionar esa decisión. Ha argumentado que una asignación a rehabilitación no habría eliminado el riesgo de lesión, y el sábado volvió a defenderla después de que se hiciera oficial su paso a la lista de lesionados.
«La gente se lesiona las pantorrillas y los cuádriceps en los partidos de rehabilitación, así que no creo que saltarse un partido en la Doble A vaya a cambiar nada de eso», dijo Judge a principios de semana.
Ahora los Yankees necesitan que Judge acepte un ritmo más lento
Judge ha construido su carrera jugando a pesar de las molestias. Se cree que la lesión en las costillas se produjo el 26 de abril en una atrapada en picado en Houston, pero siguió jugando hasta el 31 de mayo. Esa competitividad forma parte de su valor, pero ahora los Yankees tienen menos posibilidades de adaptarse a ella.
Judge se ha marcado públicamente el mes de octubre como objetivo. «Me gustaría volver para la fase final. Ese es, sin duda, el plan», dijo el sábado. Pero querer algo no es lo mismo que estar preparado. Su pantorrilla aún tiene que aguantar el esfuerzo de correr, batear y jugar partidos.
Por ahora, los Yankees siguen sin tener una respuesta. Judge se perderá la serie contra los Rays, la diferencia en la clasificación de la división es de cinco partidos y Boone no ha dicho si su capitán estará listo para cuando empiece la postemporada. La próxima decisión puede ser más importante que la anterior: hasta qué punto los Yankees dejarán que Judge se exija al máximo una vez que se recupere el sóleo.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

item.title: [bolavip.com] Aaron Boone challenges Aaron Judge-less NY Yankees ahead of Rays series
item.dc:creator: Federico O'donnell

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are down to the final inch of their slim margin of error in the 2026 MLB season. Five games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East, manager Aaron Boone didn’t mince words about how important the upcoming four-game series will be.
It will be the closest thing to a postseason series before the actual thing, and it may serve as a good opportunity for the Pinstripers to see what they are capable of doing without Aaron Judge in such a high-stakes scenario.
Although Judge and Boone kept Yankees fans concerned ahead of the postseason, the Bronx Bombers could erase those doubts with a strong showing in the four-game series against Tampa Bay. As Boone reminded his team, however, only a sweep will do them any favors.
“Oh yeah, for the division, sure [we need a sweep over the Rays]. We sweep, then it gets interesting,” Boone admitted after Saturday’s night game, per YES Network. “But we can’t sweep before [Sunday’s] game [against the Diamondbacks], so we’ve got to get ready for that game, and hopefully go out and finish what’s been a good trip out west. That’s all we can control right now.”
Aaron Judge #99 of the New York Yankees at Yankee Stadium.
Judge’s injury could demand multi-week recovery
New York isn’t giving out much information on Judge’s calf strain that landed him on the 10-day injured list (IL) only days after his return from the 60-day IL. Boone has even stated he doesn’t know the grade of Judge’s strain, which, considering how tight-lipped the Yankees remain about Judge’s injury, should be very telling on its own.
Based on the grade of the setback, the Bronx Bombers may have reason to remain confident or slowly lose all hope. In the midst of a pennant race with Tampa Bay, Bellinger all but surrendered to the Rays, though he dropped a World Series warning.
However, the story might be very different if Judge is ruled out for the rest of the season. According to reports, that remains a possibility, especially for as long as Judge’s injury grade remains unknown, or at least undisclosed to the media across MLB.
“Per the Boston Sports Medicine & Research Institute, a first-degree, or mild, calf strain comes with a 1-3-week timeline. A second-degree, or moderate, strain requires 3-6 weeks of rest and recovery before returning to full activity. A third-degree, or severe, strain ‘can take many weeks or months to fully heal.’ So I’d say it matters,” Gary Phillips of NY Daily News wrote on his X account.
Yankees vs Rays: 2026 H2H record
With four games left in the season series, Tampa Bay is 6-3 against New York, while holding a five-game lead in the race for the division. That means the Rays are only one win away from clinching the tiebreaker advantage over the Yankees, limiting Boone’s team to a sweep-or-bust scenario.
The Yankees and Rays are 1-1 at Yankee Stadium in 2026. New York’s win was a 2-0 victory resulting from a Judge two-run, walk-off homer. Clearly, the Yankees would be better off with him in the lineup when the Rays come into town.
If there’s a silver lining and sliver of hope, it is in the fact that Tampa Bay has been swept in a four-game series before this year, and it was also on the road, against the Boston Red Sox. However, that was coming out of the All-Star break, and much has changed since for the now red-hot Rays.
Regardless, anything can happen, and the AL East will be on the line when the Yankees host the Rays on Sept. 22-24 at One East 161st Street in the Bronx.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

20 Sep 2026, 13:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Arianna Grainey)
Pinch hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run, walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory over the Yankees.
Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 391-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece.
Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six.
The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the American League East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild-card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday.
White Sox 3, Tigers 1
Sean Burke hurled six quality innings and Miguel Vargas homered to help Chicago earn a victory over visiting Detroit.
Burke (10-7) allowed one run on five hits for Chicago, which remained a game behind American League Central-leading Cleveland. Sam Antonacci and Munetaka Murakami both drove in a run and Grant Taylor delivered a four-out save, his 10th overall this season.
Jackson Jobe (2-3) threw six innings of three-run, four-hit ball, striking out nine for Detroit, which remains barely alive in AL Central contention. The Tigers' wild-card elimination magic number is down to one. Kevin McGonigle drove in Detroit's lone run.
Mets 10, Phillies 3
Francisco Alvarez had two hits, including the go-ahead three-run homer in the fifth, as host New York routed skidding Philadelphia.
Carson Benge was 3-for-4 with a solo homer and two RBIs for the Mets. Brett Baty had two hits, including a run-scoring single, while Benge, Juan Soto and Bo Bichette each had RBI singles during a four-run eighth.
Alec Bohm had RBI singles in the fourth and fifth for the Phillies, who missed a chance to take over the top National League wild card, at least temporarily. The Cubs and Padres both won to remain tied atop the NL wild-card race.
Brewers 1, Orioles 0Robert Gasser pitched seven shutout innings as the first of three Milwaukee pitchers in a victory against host Baltimore.
It marked the second shutout for Milwaukee pitchers in an eight-game stretch, needing only four strikeouts for the latest accomplishment. The Brewers scored on Gary Sanchez's second-inning groundout to knock in Joey Ortiz, who tripled with one out.Baltimore has lost the first two games of the series following a three-game winning streak, further damaging its American League playoff hopes. Orioles starter Trevor Rogers (10-11) lasted eight innings, allowing one run and three hits.
Rangers 6, Blue Jays 2Texas won for the sixth time in its past seven games, defeating Toronto in Arlington, Texas.Rangers starting pitcher Cal Quantrill left the game after 1 1/3 innings with right lat tightness. Jordan Montgomery (1-0) replaced him and held Toronto hitless through 3 2/3 innings. Josh Jung gave Texas a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first with a home run to right field.Jose Soriano (12-8) gave up six runs (five earned) on four hits and struck out eight in five-plus innings for the Blue Jays, who dropped to three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final wild-card berth in the American League.
Rays 2, Red Sox 1
Richie Palacios produced a two-out, walk-off single in the ninth inning as Tampa Bay edged Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla., to even their final home series of the regular season.
Against Garrett Whitlock (7-2), Palacios looped a 1-2 sinker into right to score Junior Caminero as the Rays hit their third walk-off winner during their nine-game homestand. Jonathan Aranda homered while Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson posted two hits apiece.
Caleb Durbin stroked two doubles and scored for the Red Sox, who lost for the first time in three games. Starting pitcher Brayan Bello went a season-best eight innings and allowed one run on five hits with a career high-tying 11 strikeouts.
Guardians 12, Athletics 6
Angel Martinez homered from both sides of the plate and drove in four runs in host Cleveland's win over the Athletics which helped maintain its one-game lead in the American League Central.
Martinez was also 4-for-5 with a double and three runs scored and Chase DeLauter also homered for the Guardians, who won their fourth straight. Slade Cecconi (5-7) got the win in relief with two scoreless innings after Tanner Bibee lasted 4 2/3 innings and surrendered six runs on 12 hits.
Donovan Walton hit a home run and was 3-for-3 with four RBIs for the Athletics, who have lost five in a row. Athletics starter and loser Jacob Lopez (6-5) was blitzed for 10 runs and 10 hits in 2 2/3 innings.
Nationals 8, Cardinals 5 (11 innings)Jose Tena's two-run double keyed a four-run 11th inning and Washington beat the Cardinals in St. Louis.Jorbit Vivas had four hits and Daylen Lile homered for Washington, which has won six of seven. Riley Cornelio (3-2) pitched 1 2/3 innings for the win.At the top of the order, Jose Fermin and Ivan Herrera had three hits each for St. Louis, which has lost four straight.
Cubs 5, Reds 2
Michael Busch and Dansby Swanson hit solo home runs to lift visiting Chicago to a win over Cincinnati.
The win allowed the Cubs to pull a full game ahead of the Philadelphia Phillies for the top wild-card playoff spot in the National League. The Phillies lost 10-3 to the Mets earlier. The San Diego Padres also won to remain tied with the Cubs.
The teams will play the rubber game of the series Sunday. Cubs starter Matthew Boyd (9-5) gave up two hits and two runs (one earned) in five innings. Reds starter Nick Lodolo (3-6) gave up seven hits and three runs in seven innings.
Pirates 6, Royals 5
Brandon Lowe launched a go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to power Pittsburgh to a victory over visiting Kansas City.
Ronny Simon and Jake Mangum each hit two-run homers, while Oneil Cruz, Rafael Flores Jr. and Lowe each had two hits for the Pirates. Right-hander Luke Weaver (3-1) threw a scoreless eighth with one strikeout, and left-hander Mason Montgomery earned his 15th save of the season after working around a walk with one strikeout in a scoreless ninth.
Nick Loftin had four hits, while Bobby Witt Jr. went 3-for-5 with two runs and extended his on-base streak to 17 games for the Royals. Carter Jensen hit a solo homer, while Jac Caglianone and Vinnie Pasquantino each had two hits for Kansas City.
Braves 6, Astros 3Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a grand slam, Grant Holmes produced a quality start and Atlanta lowered its magic number to one to clinch the National League East by defeating host Houston.The Braves secured this three-game interleague series and set the table to win the NL East for the seventh time in nine seasons with a victory in the series finale on Sunday. Holmes (10-5) allowed two runs on eight hits over six innings. Closer Raisel Iglesias notched his 34th save for Atlanta.The Astros dropped a game behind the Rangers in the AL West after Texas beat Toronto. Astros reliever AJ Blubaugh (5-3) loaded the bases and was replaced by Bryan Abreu, who gave up Acuna's homer in the seventh inning for a 5-2 Braves lead.Rockies 5, Mariners 3
Cole Carrigg delivered a go-ahead two-run single in a four-run seventh inning as Colorado edged Seattle in Denver.
Juan Mejia (4-6) pitched two scoreless innings and Brennan Bernardino got the final three outs for his second save for Colorado. Jake McCarthy and TJ Rumfield each produced an RBI.
Cal Raleigh and Randy Arozarena homered and Julio Rodriguez and Michael Arroyo had two hits each for Seattle, which is on the brink of elimination in the AL wild-card race.
Padres 6, Marlins 5 (10 innings)
Rookie Ethan Salas stroked an RBI single in the bottom of the 10th inning and San Diego edged visiting Miami.
Salas' hit scored Jake Cronenworth, who started the inning as the automatic runner at second base and advanced to third on a wild pitch by Josh Ekness (2-4). David Morgan (4-1) stranded runners at first and second in the top of the 10th to earn the win, San Diego's 12th in 13 games.
The Padres tied the Chicago Cubs for the top wild-card spot in the National League at 86-69. Miami forced extra innings when pinch hitter Griffin Conine pulled a 102 mph fastball from closer Mason Miller for a game-tying homer with one out in the ninth.
Dodgers 10, Giants 4
Mookie Betts tied a season high with four hits, Tommy Edman delivered a go-ahead two-run single and Los Angeles stayed within two games of the best record in the National League with a victory over visiting San Francisco.
Betts has 10 hits over his past three games, including seven in the past two while operating out of the leadoff spot in place of an injured Shohei Ohtani. Will Smith homered as the Dodgers won for the fifth time in six games and improved to 13-3 since Sept. 3. Tarik Skubal (11-7) gave up four runs on eight hits over five innings.
Victor Bericoto hit a home run among his two hits for the Giants while Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings in his fourth career appearance and second start.
Angels 6, Twins 5 (11 innings)Christian Moore singled in automatic runner Zach Neto with a bases-loaded comebacker off pitcher Taylor Rogers' leg with two outs in the bottom of the 11th inning as Los Angeles edged Minnesota in Anaheim, Calif.Moore drilled a first-pitch sweeper that caromed off the leg of Rogers (6-4) and back toward the third base line as Neto sprinted home. Tayler Saucedo (1-1) struck out two during a scoreless inning of relief for the Angels, who tied it at 5-5 in the bottom of the ninth on Vaughn Grissom's homer.Ryan Kreidler hit a home run, Victor Caratini went 2-for-5 with two RBIs, Walker Jenkins had two hits and a run and Josh Bell and Royce Lewis each had two hits for the Twins.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [pinstripealley.com] Yankees news: Spencer Jones joins the walking wounded
item.dc:creator: Kevin Winterhalt
item.description: New York Post | Greg Joyce: The Yankees cannot afford any more additions to their M*A*S*H unit. Unfortunately, at least for Saturday, there is another. Spencer Jones, who’s been outstanding at the plate lately, was out of the starting lineup Saturday with a sore foot. For his part, Jones did not seem worried and attributed the soreness to playing in Arizona Friday after jamming his heel earlier in the week against the Twins. Here’s hoping he’s right. Yahoo Sports | Tate Mosher: Headed into what
item.content:encoded:
New York Post | Greg Joyce: The Yankees cannot afford any more additions to their M*A*S*H unit. Unfortunately, at least for Saturday, there is another. Spencer Jones, who’s been outstanding at the plate lately, was out of the starting lineup Saturday with a sore foot. For his part, Jones did not seem worried and attributed the soreness to playing in Arizona Friday after jamming his heel earlier in the week against the Twins. Here’s hoping he’s right.
Yahoo Sports | Tate Mosher: Headed into what was likely his penultimate regular season start of 2026, Cam Schlittler’s incredible campaign has the attention of people all over baseball. Cam’s been so sensational that he’s earned MVP chatter, an award that pitchers rarely hoist. The last to do it? Future Hall of Famer Clayton Kershaw. Earlier on Saturday, MLB’s official X account made sure everyone is tracking the similarities between the latter’s 2014 season and Cam’s 2026 campaign. Whether Schlittler can take home AL MVP or not, it’s been a heck of a ride. And you know you’ve had a brilliant season when you’re getting comped to Peak Kershaw.
MLB | Bryan Hoch: All Cam, all the time. The burgeoning ace has been so spectacular that it has become difficult for those closest to him to express just how good he has been. Through 31 starts, his 1.95 ERA trails only Ron Guidry’s 1.71 ERA in 1978. His 21 starts of one run or fewer are the most in franchise history. And in the past 11o years, only three pitchers his age or younger have matched him, including Babe Ruth in 1916.
CBSSports | Mike Axisa: Meanwhile, if you hadn’t heard, Aaron Judge is headed back to the IL, this time with a calf injury. In the aftermath of the Captain’s injury, Axisa takes a look at a few questions for Judge, and for the Yankees at large. For Judge, if he can return in time for a playoff run, how much has the injury set him back? Will he be able to find his timing at the dish? For the Yankees, if Judge is out or ineffective, where does that leave the offense against southpaws? It sure would be nice if Judge returns in good order and quickly finds his footing.
The Athletic | Brendan Kuty ($): Speaking of Judge’s calf injury, there’s a little bit of clarification on its nature, if not its severity or a timeline. The injury is in Judge’s inner, lower calf. That part of the calf is important for “sustained activities such as standing or walking uphill.” Judge has previously played through calf injuries. This time, however, it’s in a spot that makes doing so more difficult. So here we are, with the best hitter in the world back on the IL as the Yanks approach the postseason.

item.content:encoded:
Right-handed starting pitcher Cam Schlittler allowed three runs (one earned) on three hits and three walks while striking out six over six innings as the New York Yankees lost 5-3 to the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field in Phoenix on Saturday night.
Pavin Smith hit a walk-off two-run homer to secure the victory for Arizona.
The Yankees fell to five games behind the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the American League East after the loss.
Schlittler, the clear AL Cy Young favorite, was asked about the Yankees being five games back of the Rays.
New York Yankees Ace Cam Schlittler Makes Honest Statement After Loss to Diamondbacks
The New York Daily News’ Gary Phillips wrote on X:
Cam Schlittler on the #Yankees being 5 games behind the #Rays:
“We gotta go on a good run. It’s gonna be tough. I think we’ve had opportunities all season to put ourselves ahead, and we haven’t done a great job with it. So there’s still a chance, but we gotta play our asses off a little bit.”
Looking at the New York Yankees
The Yankees have the day off on Monday after they finish their series against the Diamondbacks on Sunday.
On Tuesday, New York is set to begin a four-game series against Tampa Bay, starting with a doubleheader.
At this point, the Yankees likely need to sweep the Rays to win the AL East. After the Rays series, the Yankees will host the Baltimore Orioles for three games, then the postseason will begin.
New York has already clinched a postseason spot, but it’s more likely the club will be a Wild Card team than a division winner.
With an 89-65 record, the Yankees are the first AL Wild Card team. They hold a 5 1/2-game lead over the Boston Red Sox, the second AL Wild Card team.
Most likely, the Yankees will host the Red Sox for a best-of-three Wild Card series. If the Yankees somehow win the AL East, they won’t have to play in the Wild Card round and will automatically earn a spot in the Division round.
The series finale of the three-game set between the Yankees and the Diamondbacks is scheduled to begin at 4:10 p.m. EDT on Sunday. Yankees fans can watch the game on the YES Network.

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] La Novia De Anthony Volpe Vuelve A Ser Noticia En Arizona Mientras La Estrella De Los Yankees Se Enfrenta A Los Diamondbacks
item.dc:creator: Inna Zeyger

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Anthony Volpe tiene muchas cosas en las que centrarse ahora que los Yankees se preparan para octubre. Su novia, Elle Jowett, por su parte, ha encontrado un rincón mucho más tranquilo de Arizona.
Jowett volvió a ser tema de conversación fuera del campo entre los Yankees el domingo, después de compartir unas fotos de una excursión por el sendero Cathedral Rock Trail, en Sedona, mientras Volpe y el equipo de Nueva York estaban en el estado para disputar su serie de tres partidos contra los Diamondbacks de Arizona.
La modelo, afincada en Nueva York, se fue de excursión a Cathedral Rock y compartió unas fotos en las que aparece meditando en el sendero. Jowett llevaba una camiseta deportiva y unos leggings mientras posaba con el característico paisaje de rocas rojas y el entorno desértico de Sedona de fondo.
El momento hace que una publicación sobre un estilo de vida que, por lo demás, sería muy sencilla, adquiera un toque relacionado con los Yankees.
Mientras Jowett disfrutaba del paisaje de Arizona, Volpe seguía inmerso en una aventura de septiembre muy diferente, a unos 190 kilómetros de distancia, en Phoenix.
Jowett sale a la luz durante una racha importante de los Yankees
Los Yankees ya se han asegurado su participación en el béisbol de octubre, tras conseguir su tercera clasificación consecutiva para la postemporada. Lo que aún está por decidir es su recorrido en la postemporada.
El sábado nos volvió a recordar que los partidos que quedan no son para tomárselos a la ligera.
Arizona venció a Nueva York por 5-3 gracias a un jonrón de dos carreras de Pavin Smith en la novena entrada que dio la victoria a su equipo. Con esta derrota, los Yankees quedan con un balance de 89-65, lo que les mantiene bajo presión en la recta final de la temporada regular.
Volpe participó de lleno en el ataque de Nueva York.
Jugó como segunda base, conectó 1 de 4, bateó un sencillo en la quinta entrada y luego anotó la primera carrera de los Yankees gracias a un fly de sacrificio de Ben Rice.
Esto convierte a la serie en otra buena prueba de fuego de octubre para un equipo de los Yankees que ya tiene asegurada su participación más allá de la temporada regular.
El papel de Volpe en los Yankees ha cambiado radicalmente
El puesto de Volpe en la alineación se ha convertido en uno de los temas más interesantes que rodean al equipo.
Los Yankees lo bajaron a la Triple A durante la segunda mitad de la temporada tras sus problemas ofensivos. Durante su etapa en las ligas menores, Volpe empezó a jugar de segunda base, alejándose de la posición de campocorto que definió sus primeros años en las Grandes Ligas.
Más tarde, Nueva York lo volvió a llamar después de que la lesión en el pulgar de Jazz Chisholm Jr. dejara un hueco en el cuadro.
Volpe anunció su regreso a lo grande el 10 de septiembre, con una actuación de tres hits y cinco carreras impulsadas, que incluyó un grand slam en la victoria de los Yankees por 10-3 sobre Colorado. Después admitió que nada de lo relacionado con su regreso estaba garantizado cuando Nueva York lo envió inicialmente a la Triple A.
Volpe está aprovechando al máximo su segunda oportunidad con los Yankees
Y lo que es más importante para los Yankees, Volpe no ha dejado que ese memorable partido de regreso sea un caso aislado.
En sus últimos ocho partidos hasta el domingo, este jugador de 25 años tenía un promedio de bateo de .296, con un porcentaje de embasado de .345 y un porcentaje de slugging de .481, lo que le da un OPS de .826. Consiguió ocho hits en 27 turnos al bate durante ese periodo, incluyendo dos dobles y un jonrón, además de impulsar siete carreras.
Esas cifras suponen una respuesta significativa por parte de un jugador cuyo futuro en los Yankees parecía mucho menos seguro cuando el club lo envió de vuelta a la Triple A.
El regreso de Volpe también vino acompañado de un cambio de posición. En lugar de recuperar inmediatamente el puesto de campocorto, ha estado jugando en segunda base mientras los Yankees evalúan cómo podría encajar su cuadro interior en octubre.
Este experimento ha añadido otra dimensión a su resurgimiento de final de temporada.
No consiguió ningún hit en sus cuatro turnos al bate durante la victoria del viernes por 9-2 contra Arizona, pero el sábado respondió con un sencillo y una carrera anotada.
La tendencia general sigue siendo alentadora.
Volpe llegó a esta recta final con la necesidad de demostrar que su paso por la Triple A había dado frutos tangibles. En lugar de volver simplemente porque una lesión le había dejado un hueco, ha empezado a dar a los Yankees motivos para seguir dándole oportunidades al bate.
Eso podría ser muy importante cuando el entrenador Aaron Boone empiece a decidir qué combinación de infield le da a Nueva York su mejor alineación para la postemporada.
Elle Jowett ha ido acaparando cada vez más la atención de los Yankees
La aparición de Jowett en Arizona no es la primera vez que su actividad en las redes sociales llama la atención en un momento importante de la temporada de Volpe.
Ella y Volpe se hicieron públicos como pareja durante la temporada de 2025 tras aparecer juntos en la gala Willow Grant de la Fundación Carlos Rodón en Greenwich, Connecticut.
Posteriormente, Jowett asistió a partidos de la postemporada de los Yankees, aunque la pareja ha mantenido en general su relación al margen de sus propias redes sociales.
A principios de este año, Jowett volvió a aparecer en los titulares tras compartir fotos de Los Ángeles más o menos cuando los Yankees enviaron a Volpe a la Triple A. Otros miembros de la gran familia de los Yankees interactuaron con esa publicación.
Más tarde, llamó la atención con otra publicación de modelaje coincidiendo con el regreso de Volpe a las Grandes Ligas.
Ahora, Arizona es el último punto de encuentro entre los mundos separados de la pareja.
El fin de semana de Jowett ha girado en torno a la meditación y al paisaje de rocas rojas de Sedona. El de Volpe, por su parte, ha estado marcado por un equipo de los Yankees , que se dirige a la postemporada, que ha tenido que lidiar con una derrota en la última entrada, un panorama cambiante en el cuadro y decisiones cada vez más importantes sobre su alineación para octubre.
Los contextos no podrían ser más diferentes.
Pero ahora que octubre está a la vuelta de la esquina, ambas han vuelto a poner la vida fuera del campo de Volpe al mismo nivel que uno de los tramos más decisivos de su temporada con los Yankees.
¿Qué le parece? Deje su comentario a continuación.

item.title: [bolavip.com] NY Yankees’ Cody Bellinger all but surrenders to Rays, yet drops World Series warning
item.dc:creator: Federico O'donnell
item.description: The New York Yankees lost the second game against the Arizona Diamondbacks by a score of 5-3. The fact that the loss came on the heels of Aaron Boone keeping Yankees fans concerned about Aaron Judge ahead of the MLB Postseason didn’t help. The fact that it widened the Tampa Bay Rays‘ lead over the Pinstripers for first place in the AL East wasn’t great, either. Still, Cody Bellinger believes in his team. item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees lost the second game against the Arizona Diamondbacks by a score of 5-3. The fact that the loss came on the heels of Aaron Boone keeping Yankees fans concerned about Aaron Judge ahead of the MLB Postseason didn’t help. The fact that it widened the Tampa Bay Rays‘ lead over the Pinstripers for first place in the AL East wasn’t great, either. Still, Cody Bellinger believes in his team.
Apparently, not enough to be convinced that the Yankees may still make it a pennant race with the Rays and come away on top, but he sure is confident that once the postseason arrives, the Bronx Bombers can turn it up a notch. And who knows? Why not win the World Series?
It’s happened before, and the Yankees have already received a good omen from the New York Giants and New York Jets. The signs may be out there. In case they aren’t clear enough, Bellinger’s latest statement might help out even more. The Rays, and frankly, the entire MLB landscape, have been put on notice.
“Yeah, I mean, [the Rays] are playing tremendous baseball. It’s tough to climb up in the standings if they keep winning. Mathematically pretty tough, we have got to keep on rolling,” Bellinger said postgame, via YES Network. “Obviously, the goal is win the division, rest your guys, get those extra off days, that’s always goal No. 1. Ultimately, World Series champions have come out of the Wild Card.”
Decisive Rays-Yankees series
Although Bellinger’s admission after the defeat in Phoenix sounded almost like the Yankees were waving the white flag in the pennant race against the Rays, there is still some baseball left to play, and a couple of very meaningful games on the horizon. New York and Tampa Bay will meet for a four-game series at Yankee Stadium (Sept. 22-24, with a doubleheader on Sept. 22) that could very well decide who wins the American League East division.
If the Boston Red Sox can get a win in the rubber match against the Rays while the Yankees secure the series against the D-Backs, then a sweep by New York against Tampa Bay would put both teams at even-Stevens. A sweep is the only way for the Yankees to get the tiebreaker over the Rays, as they are currently down 3-6 in the season’s head-to-head.
Another Rays win over the Pinstripers will clinch the tiebreaker for them. It’s a tough ask for New York, but not impossible. Obviously, without Judge, the climb is only steeper, but it may be perfect timing for a new miracle in the Bronx.
NY Yankees and TB Rays’ remaining schedule
| Games left | NY Yankees | TB Rays |
| One game vs | Arizona D-Backs | Boston Red Sox |
| Four games vs | TB Rays | NY Yankees |

item.title: [Empire Sports Media] Yankees' ace just crashed the Cy Young race
item.dc:creator: Alexander Wilson
item.description: The Yankees got walked off in Phoenix on Friday. Cam Schlittler was not the reason why. He gave them six innings, one earned run and six strikeouts before the game got away late. At some point, it gets silly to keep calling this a nice first season in the majors. Schlittler has a 1.94 ERA, a 0.91 WHIP and 234 strikeouts across 190 2/3 innings. A line like that belongs at the front of a rotation, and it is happening while everyone is busy checking other names in the award race. I am done treating
item.content:encoded:
The Yankees got walked off in Phoenix on Friday. Cam Schlittler was not the reason why. He gave them six innings, one earned run and six strikeouts before the game got away late.
At some point, it gets silly to keep calling this a nice first season in the majors. Schlittler has a 1.94 ERA, a 0.91 WHIP and 234 strikeouts across 190 2/3 innings. A line like that belongs at the front of a rotation, and it is happening while everyone is busy checking other names in the award race.
I am done treating him like a cute September development. The Yankees have an ace who is already pitching like he belongs in the Cy Young mix.
Friday also put him in unusual company. Schlittler has now allowed one earned run or fewer in 24 starts, an absurdly steady run for a pitcher carrying a real workload.
Why the Yankees’ ace belongs in the Cy Young race
Schlittler has not built the case on one monster outing or a couple of easy matchups. The workload and strikeouts stand up, while the traffic has stayed low enough that even a rough bullpen finish cannot hide how good the starter was again.
The usual experience gap applies. Voters will have other pitchers with longer track records, and awards can become a name-recognition contest when the numbers are close. Still, a 1.94 ERA after nearly 200 innings does not need a sales pitch.
Friday did not damage the argument
The final score will bother Yankees fans more than Schlittler’s line. Arizona beat New York 5-3 on Pavin Smith’s ninth-inning homer, but the loss did not undo what the right-hander gave the club.
Schlittler should get the next start with more than a pat on the back. He has given the Yankees a legitimate Cy Young candidate, and he is making that claim harder to dismiss every five days.
More about:New York Yankees

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] Cam Schlittler Lanza Un Mensaje Contundente A Los Yankees Mientras La Derrota Ante Arizona Agrava Los Problemas En La División Este De La Liga Americana
item.dc:creator: Esteban Quiñones

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Cam Schlittler se fue del Chase Field con otra actuación como lanzador que se consideraría dominante en casi cualquier otro sitio. Para los Yankees, fue otro recordatorio de que un as solo puede compensar hasta cierto punto cuando el margen a su alrededor no deja de reducirse.
Schlittler limitó a Arizona a tres hits y una carrera limpia en seis entradas el sábado por la noche, ponchando a seis y concediendo tres bases por bolas. Aun así , los Yankees perdieron por 5-3 cuando Pavin Smith conectó un jonrón de dos carreras como bateador suplente ante Michael Fulmer en la novena entrada, lo que convirtió un partido empatado en la undécima derrota de Nueva York en la última entrada de la temporada.
Con esta derrota, los Yankees quedan con un balance de 89-65 y a cinco partidos del Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, cuando solo quedan ocho partidos por disputar. Nueva York ya se ha asegurado una plaza en la postemporada, pero el camino hacia el título de división pasa ahora por cuatro partidos contra los Rays en el Yankee Stadium y necesitará algo de ayuda más allá de esa serie.
La actuación de Schlittler hizo que el resultado fuera más difícil de pasar por alto como una simple derrota de septiembre. Su promedio de carreras limpias bajó hasta 1,94, el mejor de la Liga Americana, y sus estadísticas de la temporada quedaron en 14-6, con 234 strikeouts en 190 2/3 entradas. Terminó su gira con un promedio de carreras limpias de 1,16 en 17 partidos como titular.
Los Yankees le dieron una ventaja momentánea de 3-2 en la sexta entrada gracias a dos jonrones solitarios de Heliot Ramos y Austin Wells. Schlittler empezó entonces la parte baja de la entrada con ocho bolas seguidas, Geraldo Perdomo conectó un sencillo de toque y un fly de sacrificio de Corbin Carroll empató el partido. Antes, un error de Schlittler en la defensa ante un toque de Tim Tawa ayudó a que Jordan Lawlar conectara un triple de dos carreras.
Juan Morillo se llevó la victoria tras lanzar 1 1/3 entradas sin permitir ningún hit con Arizona. Fulmer se llevó la derrota después de que Ildemaro Vargas ganara una revisión de ABS por una base por bolas al primer bateador en la novena y Smith mandara un cutter a las gradas del campo derecho. No hubo salvamento.
Así pues, Schlittler había sumado seis entradas más de excelente control de carreras sin cambiar el problema general de los Yankees. Nueva York acabó con un balance de 20-12 en sus 32 salidas como titular, un balance poco habitual para un equipo que solo ha encajado una carrera limpia o menos en 24 de esas salidas.
La racha histórica de no encajar carreras sigue adentrándose en un terreno cada vez más excepcional
La derrota no frenó el ascenso de Schlittler en las estadísticas. Según la investigación histórica de Sarah Langs, Schlittler acumuló 24 salidas en las que no permitió más de una carrera limpia, lo que le sitúa empatado con Bob Gibson en 1968 y Sandy Koufax en 1966 en el segundo puesto de la «Era de la Bola Viva». Koufax llegó a 25 en 1963.
En la historia de la Liga Americana, solo Walter Johnson logró más salidas de este tipo en una temporada: 27 en 1913 y 26 en 1914. El promedio de carreras limpias permitidas (ERA) de Schlittler a domicilio, de 1,16, solo queda por detrás del 1,06 de Johnson en 1913 entre los lanzadores de la Liga Americana con al menos 15 salidas como visitante.
Su trayectoria profesional es casi igual de impresionante. En sus primeras 45 salidas como titular en las Grandes Ligas, antes del sábado, Schlittler sumaba 312 strikeouts y una ERA de 2,24. Según los datos históricos que nos han facilitado, se sitúa junto a José Fernández y Paul Skenes como los únicos lanzadores que han superado los 300 ponches sin superar una efectividad de 2,30 hasta ese momento.
Schlittler tiene ahora una media de carreras limpias permitidas (ERA) de 2,22 en su carrera, con 318 strikeouts en 46 partidos como titular. Además, está intentando unirse a Ron Guidry en 1978 y a Spud Chandler en 1943 como los únicos lanzadores titulares de los Yankees de la «era de la bola viva» que han terminado una temporada con una efectividad por debajo de 2,00.
Schlittler lanza un mensaje contundente
No fue hasta después del partido cuando Schlittler pasó de hablar de sus propias estadísticas de lanzamiento a hablar de la posición de los Yankees en la clasificación. Cuando le preguntaron por la diferencia de cinco partidos, hizo un análisis directo de una carrera en la que Nueva York ha tenido varias oportunidades de recortar distancias.
«Tenemos que encadenar una buena racha. Va a ser duro. Creo que hemos tenido oportunidades durante toda la temporada para ponernos por delante, y no las hemos aprovechado muy bien. Así que todavía hay posibilidades, pero tenemos que darlo todo».
El mensaje cobró aún más importancia porque Schlittler acababa de asumir la responsabilidad de la jugada que le había cambiado el comienzo del partido. No utilizó las dos carreras no ganadas como excusa para que los Yankees perdieran otro partido que necesitaban ganar.
«Bueno, no diría que les di una oportunidad de verdad», dijo Schlittler. «Eso es culpa mía, así que asumo la responsabilidad. Cometí un error ahí y les dejé marcar dos carreras».
Reiteró esa idea unos instantes después, en lugar de echarle la culpa a la defensa, al bullpen o a la alineación.
«Bueno, así es el béisbol, pero sí, esa la pago yo».
Una jugada maestra más podría decidir cómo empieza octubre
Un gráfico comparativo de la MLB publicado antes del sábado situaba la temporada de Schlittler al mismo nivel que la de Clayton Kershaw en 2014, cuando fue MVP, y la de Justin Verlander en 2011, también como MVP. Esa comparación refleja hasta qué punto su candidatura ha ido más allá de la típica discusión sobre el premio Cy Young, aunque la carrera por el MVP siga siendo otra historia.
Para los Yankees, lo más importante ahora mismo es octubre. Los Yankees pueden armar su rotación para la postemporada en torno a Schlittler, que está listo para encabezar esa rotación, y Nueva York puede alinearlo para una salida más en la temporada regular, posiblemente contra Tampa Bay durante la serie de cuatro partidos que empieza el martes.
Su valoración sin rodeos después de que Arizona demostrara más que nadie la urgencia del momento. Los Yankees siguen contando con su mejor lanzador, que está rindiendo a un nivel histórico. Lo que sigue siendo una incógnita es si le han dejado suficientes partidos para dar un giro a la lucha por el título de división.
¿Qué opinas? Deja tu comentario más abajo.

item.title: [arkansasonline.com] A Beloved Species Of September Nears Extinction. How the Game Is Forcing Out Pinch-Runners. | Arkansas Democrat Gazette
item.dc:creator: Chad Jennings The Athletic

item.content:encoded:
Rudy Martin Jr. waited 12 years for an opportunity that lasted three days. And the shame of it is, he never really got to run.
Called up by the Toronto Blue Jays last Friday, Martin was wearing a big league uniform for the first time at age 30. He had been drafted in 2014 and played stints in Mexico and two independent leagues before the Blue Jays decided a guy with 45 stolen bases in 91 minor league games might help them make the MLB playoffs.
Martin pinch-ran last Friday, he played seven innings Saturday, and he went on the injured list with a strained hamstring Monday. He never went first to third, never scored on a sacrifice fly, never attempted to steal second base. There is little guarantee he will ever get another chance.
But 10 years ago, his chances would have been annual events.
Martin was, for one weekend, a throwback to a not-so-distant era when anonymous minor leaguers arrived every September and made big league names for themselves with their speed. Some of those September call-ups eventually established long careers, turning exciting moments as stretch-run pinch-runners into lasting big league paychecks.
Martin might have been one of those annual call-ups, but he did not reach Class AAA until 2019, the year before MLB limited September call-ups to two players per team, effectively condemning September pinch-runners to near extinction, and making it harder for anyone to run so fast that major league teams simply could not ignore them.
"Having speed and chasing the playoffs definitely had a big impact and gave me more opportunities than I would if I did not have this speed," Atlanta Braves first-base coach Antoan Richardson said.
Richardson got to the big leagues twice as a player, each time as a September call-up for a team in contention. He debuted with Atlanta in 2011, then he scored the winning run on Derek Jeter's final Yankee Stadium at-bat in 2014. Jeter's much-replayed walk-off single featured a player with only 20 career at-bats.
Under the old rules, players like Richardson arrived every September. But these days, having one tool is no longer enough for such specialized, game-changing players to get a foot in the door.
"Call-ups in September have changed completely," said Tim Locastro, who ran his way onto a big league roster in 2017.
For decades, September rosters could expand to 40 players. Teams rarely activated that many, but 30-plus was typical, and clubhouses became overcrowded with redundancy and specialization. One-dimensional pinch-runners were not the only September luxury. Third catchers were standard, and top prospects were often promoted despite having little to do but get acclimated to the major leagues -- in 1993, Atlanta called up 21-year-old Chipper Jones and gave him three at-bats.
One major league executive, granted anonymity to speak candidly, noted that the widespread youth and athleticism of modern rosters could be a contributing factor in the decline of September runners -- teams do not necessarily need to pinch-run as often -- but said that the 28-man roster limit was surely the main reason so few teams seem interested in finding the next Terrance Gore.
Last year's Los Angeles Dodgers carried Justin Dean as a dedicated late-season pinch-runner and defensive replacement, but the Dodgers, with their unusual depth, are outliers. Few other teams feel they can devote a roster spot to such a limited player.
There was a brief attempt, a half-century ago, to make pinch-running a season-long occupation. The Oakland Athletics of the 1960s and 1970s regularly gave roster spots to players whose main job, or only job, was to pinch-run. Allan Lewis, Don Hopkins, Matt Alexander and Larry Lintz rarely did much else for the A's, but they did a lot of running, and their teams did a lot of winning. Most famous of the team's runners was Herb Washington, an international track star with a minimal baseball background who never hit or played the field but got into 92 games and stole 29 bases in 1974 as the A's won their third consecutive World Series.
Despite the A's success, their designated runner strategy did not catch on, and even the team's owner, Charlie Finley, seemed to lose interest in the idea (though the Pittsburgh Pirates did sign Alexander and use him in much the same way on the way to their own championship in 1979). September roster expansion, though, allowed the concept to survive as an annual, one-month-only tradition.
September call-ups in the 1980s and 1990s often included running specialists -- from Jeff Stone with the Philadelphia Phillies in 1983 to Eddie Miller for the San Diego Padres in 1984 -- but the practice spiked with the data-driven strategy of the 2000s. In 2009, 13 players stole at least 30 bases in Class AAA, and 12 of them were on major league rosters come September. Only one of the dozen had previously spent more than a couple of weeks in the big leagues. Class AAA leaderboards at that time were always littered with September call-ups.
In 2013, the Cincinnati Reds used September expansion to call up 22-year-old Billy Hamilton, who promptly stole 13 bases in 13 games to help the Reds clinch the final wild-card spot in the National League. Two years later, the Atlanta Braves gave a September call-up to 31-year-old Emilio Bonifácio, whom they had designated for assignment just two months earlier. In 2017, Locastro made his major league debut in September and got his first of 29 consecutive stolen bases without being caught, an MLB record for the start of a career.
"That year I got called up in 2017, all August in the minor leagues, I'm trying to show my speed off more than anything," Locastro said. "I knew if I was going to be called up, it was going to be to run the bases."
Some had memorable names -- Esix Snead, Rico Noel, Charlton Jimerson -- but few had notable careers beyond the fact that in the right moment, they could bring a stadium to its feet. Yet the nature of their jobs made them unforgettable to every fan base that got to see them run.
Most famous of the September runners was Gore, who got to the big leagues every year from 2014 to 2022, won three World Series rings with three organizations and became such a Kansas City Royals icon that his death in February prompted online tributes and an opening day ceremony. Gore started only 14 major league games in his career. But he played in 123, including 11 in the postseason; more than half of Gore's appearances came in September, and his only big league action in 2021 was as an Atlanta pinch-runner in a division series. Baseball Reference considers Gore to have 0.1 wins above replacement, but he stole 43 bases, and most of them came off the bench, late in the year, for playoff-bound teams.
"There have been very few players who can take over a baseball game," Dayton Moore, a former Royals general manager, said after Gore died. "That's exactly what he did."
The Class AAA steals leaders this year, Braiden Ward and Duke Ellis, are experienced outfielders in the Red Sox and Yankees farm systems, each with 50-plus steals and their parent clubs in contention.
That was a reliable call-up formula a decade ago, but neither has been promoted. To get Martin on the roster last week, the Blue Jays had to designate for assignment an underperforming veteran, Jesus Sanchez. The call-up was not as simple as putting Martin on the 40-man roster and stitching his name onto a jersey.
Nearly a decade after the September call-up that started his own big league career, Locastro now works as a minor league instructor with the Padres, and part of his job is to teach young players to run the bases. But he has to warn them: Running cannot be all they do.
"Nowadays," Locastro said, "you need to have all aspects of the game if you want to be called up in September."

item.title: [nydailynews.com] Yankees’ division dreams hanging by a thread after walk-off loss: ‘It’s gonna be tough’
item.dc:creator: Gary Phillips
item.description: PHOENIX — Both the Yankees and Rays saw their respective games end in walk-off fashion on Saturday, but only one of the division rivals emerged victorious. It wasn’t the Yanks, who suffered a 5-3 loss to the Diamondbacks when Michael Fulmer surrendered a game-ending, two-run home to Pavin Smith with one out in the ninth inning. item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Both the Yankees and Rays saw their respective games end in walk-off fashion on Saturday, but only one of the division rivals emerged victorious.
It wasn’t the Yanks, who suffered a 5-3 loss to the Diamondbacks when Michael Fulmer surrendered a game-ending, two-run home to Pavin Smith with one out in the ninth inning. Aaron Boone said that he considered using Clarke Schmidt, one game back from Tommy John surgery, instead, but he went with the journeyman Fulmer because he’s had more experience in those situations.
“I just felt like Fulmer’s been in these spots and throwing the ball really well for us, and Smith got him there,” Boone said of the reliever, who has a 3.09 ERA this season.
Meanwhile, at Tropicana Field, the Rays pulled off a 2-1 win over the Red Sox thanks to a bloop single from Richie Palacios in the ninth. Tampa now has a five-game lead over the Yankees with just eight games left in the regular season.
The American League East foes will play four of those games against each other at Yankee Stadium from Sept. 22-24, starting with a doubleheader on Tuesday. Boone acknowledged that his club will probably have to sweep the Rays for a crack at a division title.
“We sweep, then it gets interesting,” the manager said with the Yankees’ postseason ticket already punched.
But the odds are already stacked against the Yankees with the team finishing its series in Arizona on Sunday. They entered Saturday with a just a 2.8% chance of winning the division, according to FanGraphs.
Making matters tougher is that the Rays, owners of the AL’s best record, currently lead the season series between the two teams, 6-3. There’s also the fact that the Yankees will be without Aaron Judge, who returned to the injured list with calf strain on Saturday.
“They’re playing tremendous baseball, so it’s tough to climb up in the standings when they keep winning,” Cody Bellinger said after going 0-for-4 on Saturday. “So mathematically, it’s pretty tough, but gotta keep on rolling.”
“We gotta go on a good run. It’s gonna be tough,” added Cam Schlittler, who allowed one earned run over six innings but committed a costly error on Saturday. “I think we’ve had opportunities all season to put ourselves ahead, and we haven’t done a great job with it. So there’s still a chance, but we gotta play our asses off a little bit.”
The good news for the Yankees is that their best starters are lined up to face the Rays. While they haven’t officially announced their probables for the series, it looks like Max Fried and Carlos Rodón will pitch the doubleheader before Gerrit Cole and Schlittler, the Cy Young frontrunner, close out the four-game set.
The Rays, however, are set to throw a few of their best with Drew Rasmussen, Nick Martinez, Ian Seymour and Freddy Peralta slotted for the highly-anticipated matchup.
While they’re not officially out of the division race yet, the likeliest scenario is that the Yankees end up hosting Boston in the Wild Card round for the second straight year. It is not where the team wants to end up after finishing 2025 with the same record as the Blue Jays but losing the season series tiebreaker, but Bellinger remained confident that the Yankees can still win their first title since 2009.
“Obviously, the goal is to win the division, rest your guys, get those extra off days,” he said. “That’s always goal No. 1. Ultimately, World Series champions have come out of the Wild Card.”

Alec Bohm had a pair of run-scoring singles and Bryce Harper delivered a sacrifice fly for the Phillies, who entered Saturday tied with the Chicago Cubs and San Di
item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK -- Carson Benge had three hits to break Pete Alonso's Mets season rookie record, homering along with Francisco Alvarez as New York again prevented the Philadelphia Phillies from gaining ground in the National League wild card race with a 10-3 win Saturday.
Benge raised his hits total to 156, one more than Pete Alonso in 2019.
Alec Bohm had a pair of run-scoring singles and Bryce Harper delivered a sacrifice fly for the Phillies, who entered Saturday tied with the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres for the three NL wild cards, five games ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks.
Alvarez's three-run home run off Andrew Painter (3-10) put the Mets ahead for good in the fifth.
Benge doffed his cap to an ovation from the crowd of 37,468 following the record-breaking hit, an RBI infield single in the eighth.
CUBS 5, REDS 2 Matthew Boyd ended a six-start winless streak, Dansby Swanson hit his first home run since coming off the injured list and visiting Chicago moved closer to its second consecutive playoff berth by beating Cincinnati. Michael Busch hit a tiebreaking home run off Nick Lodolo (3-6) in the sixth inning for a 3-2 lead, reaching 20 home runs for the third time in four seasons. Swanson added a ninth-inning drive against Zach McCambley, his first since Aug. 12.
NATIONALS 8, CARDINALS 5 (11) Washington scored four runs in the top of the 11th inning to break a 4-4 tie, then worked out of a bases-loaded jam with no outs in the bottom of the inning to get by host St. Louis. Jose Terra hit a two-run double to break the game open, giving the Nationals a 7-4 lead. Dylan Crews' sacrifice fly scored Jacob Young to make it 8-4. JJ Wetherholt hit an RBI single in the bottom of the inning to provide the final margin.
AMERICAN LEAGUE
RANGERS 6, BLUE JAYS 3 Five relievers held Toronto to six hits after Cal Quantrill left 12 pitches in because of right lat tightness, and Texas moved into sole possession of the AL West lead for the first time since late August with a win over visiting Toronto. Texas has won six of seven and moved a half-game ahead of Houston, which holds the tiebreaker. The Rangers have a winning record for the first time since before play on Aug. 11.
WHITE SOX 3, TIGERS 1 Sean Burke pitched six effective innings, Miguel Vargas homered and Chicago topped visiting Detroit. The White Sox dropped at least 101 games in each of the last three years. They could become the first big league team to make the playoffs after finishing with at least 100 losses in each of the previous two seasons. Burke (10-7) allowed one run and five hits in his second consecutive win. Grant Taylor got four outs for his 10th save.
RAYS 2, RED SOX 1 Richie Palacios dropped a fly ball into shallow right in the ninth inning to score Junior Caminero and give Tampa Bay a victory over visiting Boston. The Rays, who've won seven of their last eight, capitalized on two fortuitous bounces in the ninth. First, Caminero's foul popup bounced off the Tropicana Field catwalk and out of the reach of third baseman Caleb Durbin. Caminero then lined the next pitch from Garrett Whitlock (7-2) into left. Three batters later, after Chandler Simpson singled, Connor Wong's passed ball moved Caminero to third.
GUARDIANS 12, ATHLETICS 6 Angel Martínez homered from both sides of the plate and had his second career four-hit game, Chase DeLauter had a three-run home run, and host Cleveland remained in first place in the AL Central with a victory over the Athletics.
INTERLEAGUE
BRAVES 6, ASTROS 3 Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a go-ahead grand slam in the seventh inning, and visiting Atlanta beat Houston to drop the Astros out of the AL West lead. Trailing 2-1, Atlanta loaded the bases against AJ Blubaugh (5-3) and Acuna homered off Bryan Abreu for his second grand slam this season and the fifth of his big league career. Acuna singled and walked twice in his first three plate appearances. He has homered in three of his last four games.
BREWERS 1, ORIOLES 0 Visiting Milwaukee tied a team record with their 97th win of the season, beating Baltimore with the help of a fly ball lost in the sun by Orioles right fielder Rece Hinds. Hinds lost Joey Ortiz's fly ball in the sun in the second inning and tumbled to the ground, and Gary Sánchez hit into a run-scoring groundout.
PIRATES 6, ROYALS 5 Brandon Lowe hit a go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth to lift host Pittsburgh to a victory over Kansas City. Lowe jumped on a pitch from Steven Cruz (2-4) and sent it into the seats in right field for his 33rd home run of the season, the second-most by a player in their first year with the Pirates.
ROCKIES 5, MARINERS 3 Host Colorado used a four-run seventh inning to earn a victory over Seattle. The Mariners built a 3-0 lead, thanks to a two-run home run from Cal Raleigh in the first and a solo shot from Randy Arozarena in the third. Cole Carigg hit a two-run single in the seventh that gave the lead to Colorado, which got an RBI single from TJ Rumfield to tie the game at 3-3 earlier in the inning.
DIAMONDBACKS 5, YANKEES 3 Pavin Smith hit a two-run home run to right-center field in the bottom of the ninth inning to give host Arizona a victory over New York. Jordan Lawlar's triple in the bototm of the fifth scored Nolan Arenado to give Arizona a 2-1 lead, but Heliot Ramos hit a solo home run in the sixth to tie the game at 2-2. Austin Wells hit a home run later in the inning, giving New York the lead, but Arizona tied the game in the bottom of the inning when Ketel Marte scored on Corbin Carroll's sacrifice fly.

item.title: [courant.com] Dom Amore’s Sunday Read: Coach that launched Sun has his day; big skates to fill at UConn, and more
item.dc:creator: Dom Amore
item.description: Mike Thibault was with the Lakers during the early 1980s “Showtime” period, and he was with the Bulls when they drafted Michael Jordan. Then he moved around to different leagues, circumstances, and went back to the NBA as a Bucks assistant.
