item.content:encoded:
WELCOME TO THE EVENING SHADE, A SANCTUARY OF SANITY AFTER A LONG HARD DAY OF FIGHTING FASCISM.
YOU WILL FIND in the DIARIES a LOT of POLITICS (Or NOT As the CASE MAY BE) AND EVEN MORE CRITTERS. THE PERSON who MAKES the FIRST COMMENT WILL GET TWO CRITTERS. EVERY PERSON WHO COMMENTS WILL GET A CRITTER (OR LYNX TO A CRITTER)
The good news is that I found a trove of 50+ comics this morning. The bad news is that it took me a long time to get them set aside. I’m going to have to just categorize them and put them in a Google Doc for the other diarists to use what I don’t.
I’m way behind schedule.
News
The Guardian
A federal immigration officer wanted on assault charges for shooting and wounding a Venezuelan man in Minneapolis was arrested there on Wednesday, eight months after a confrontation that became a flashpoint over Donald Trump’s deportation sweeps.
Christian Castro, an Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent, was taken into custody by agents of the Minnesota bureau of criminal apprehension in Minneapolis and was booked into the Hennepin county jail on his outstanding arrest warrant, the agency said.
Castro had been released on bond from federal custody earlier this month, after an initial appearance in a district court in McAllen, Texas, on charges of lying to investigators about the circumstances of the 14 January shooting.
Under an agreement with Minnesota law enforcement, Castro voluntarily drove to Minneapolis from Texas to turn himself in to state authorities at his attorney’s office but ended up being arrested minutes before he was due to arrive, the lawyer, Daniel Gerdts, told Reuters.
Minnesota’s Moriarty and Ellison are pushing back against the assertion in the last paragraph that Castro had an agreement. Mary Moriarty said that Castro didn’t get to set the time and place of his arrest. That’s a weird flex that Castro and his lawyer were trying to pull.
This isn’t one of the killers (that I know of) in the Twin Cities last winter. Not for lack of trying. He shot into a residence and his bullet lodged in the bedroom wall where a child was. Then Castro and his partner lied about the incident until video emerged. The US Attorney then dropped all charges against the victims and Castro fled to Texas, into the warm, loving embrace of Greg Abbott, who wouldn’t willingly give up his boy-toy.
===
Nifty gave us an upbeat story of a similar ilk (but before Chicago’s own occupation) in the comments of yesterday’s GNR. Note that these crimes occurred before Chicago’s Midway Blitz.
Chicago Sun Times
It simply didn’t matter whether Luis Uribe’s victims were sex workers.
That’s what a prosecutor told jurors this week when he asked for a guilty verdict against the U.S. Customs and Border Protection officer who used his gun and badge to commit violent sexual assaults.
It’s possible for a sex worker to be raped, Assistant U.S. Attorney Richard Rothblatt reminded the jury. For them to be robbed. “Sex workers,” he said, “can be credible.”
The jury agreed Thursday, siding with four women over a federal law enforcement officer whose lawyer called the victims “liars” and “hustlers.” The panel concluded that Uribe, 45, sexually assaulted the women in Chicago’s suburbs in 2022, convicting him of a series of crimes that could put him in prison for the rest of his life.
They also rejected Uribe’s claim that he’d been set up by a Chinese prostitution ring because he wouldn’t help them circumvent U.S. immigration law — an explanation Uribe delivered from the witness stand amid testimony in which he was accused of telling a “rape joke.” ✂️
It’s a disturbing story. It reinforces that there needs to be reform of ICE and CBP.
===
===
Since we’ve shifted to Chicago, Kat Abughazaleh has a book about organizing that drops as a free download on Monday. You can get a hard (spiral bound) copy for a $50 or more donation. Or as I call it, less than the price of a tank of gas.
Here’s the link to the download. Here’s the link to the donation page for the PAC for those that want a hard copy ($50 or more donation).
===
Michigan Advance
The family of a woman who died after she could not get an abortion in Texas is suing doctors and state officials including Attorney General Ken Paxton. It is the first lawsuit over a death linked to an abortion ban.
“It’s horrible that she’s gone and she was taken from us this way. It’s horrible that she’s not here anymore,” said LaTanya Walker, Tierra Walker’s aunt and the lead plaintiff in the case, in a press conference Wednesday. She added: “I want justice for her. I want it to not happen to anyone else. It needs to stop.”
The case, filed Tuesday in state court by a malpractice firm and the abortion rights group Amplify Legal, argues that Texas’ abortion bans violate both the state and U.S. Constitution. This case is also the first to directly sue Paxton, who has taken a leading role in enforcing Texas’ ban. Paxton is locked in a tight race for the U.S. Senate.
“Tierra Walker is dead and those responsible must be held accountable,” the suit reads. “At every turn, Texas’s political and medical establishments not only failed but actively harmed Ms. Walker.”
Walker is one of the numerous women whose deaths have been linked to abortion bans. Other deaths have occurred in North Carolina and Georgia, states with bans less restrictive than Texas’. Texas’ near-total abortion ban provides exceptions only if staying pregnant puts someone “at risk of death or poses a serious risk of substantial impairment of a major bodily function.” In 2025 — after Walker’s death — the state passed a law meant to clarify what constitutes a risk of death. But the penalties for violating the state’s ban remain onerous, and many doctors have said it is not obvious what care they can provide or how sick a patient must be before they can intervene. ✂️
===
===
Hat tip to Girasol for the heads up on this next item.
Boise State Public Radio
Parent company McClatchy Media laid off 10 journalists and three editors at the Idaho Statesman on Thursday.
Michael Lycklama, chair of the Idaho News Guild, the union representing most Statesman reporters, said that’s 60% of the newsroom.
Lycklama was a sports reporter for the paper for 12 years. He said he got an email Thursday morning notifying him of an HR meeting 30 minutes later.
“That was all the notice that I got, and got a nonsensical explanation that didn’t explain any reasons why they’re doing the things that they’re doing,” he said.
McClatchy laid off staff in newsrooms across the country. An exact count is unknown, but Poynter reports at least 90 journalists have been affected across 13 papers.
The New York Times reports McClatchy told employees subscriber revenue had fallen 41%. A layoff notice McClatchy sent to union leadership and shared with Boise State Public Radio listed shifting subscriber interests and changes in the ways people engage with news as the reason for its restructuring. The company said it is focusing resources on journalism, subscriber value and what serves local communities. ✂️
===
Virginia Mercury
Gov. Abigail Spanberger on Friday unveiled a package of legislative proposals to rein in the data center industry in Virginia, with goals to tighten environmental regulations, increase cost allocation for the industry, and make the proposal process more transparent by barring non-disclosure agreements between localities and data center developers.
The plan does not include a moratorium on data center development while the details of the plan are refined, a step several environmental and advocacy groups and citizens have demanded in recent weeks.
Dubbed the “Data Center Accountability Framework,” Spanberger’s plan outlines five pillars as key priorities: transparency, environmental protections, lowering energy costs, promoting clean energy, and focusing on local workers.
“The Framework is a thorough plan to end data center secrecy, protect our environment, lower energy costs for families, bolster our clean energy economy, and make sure Virginia workers have the protections and assurances they deserve,” Spanberger said in a press conference to announce the plan at the Virginia State Capitol.
Spanberger also signed Executive Order 22, which will kick-start her plans for clamping down on the industry ahead of the next legislative session that will begin in January 2027. ✂️
===
===
Alaska Beacon
On the day that his campaign announced it had accepted hundreds of thousands of dollars in donations from employees of a California-based artificial intelligence company, Democratic governor candidate Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins said that if elected, he will seek to temporarily ban new computing data centers in Alaska.
As Americans grow frustrated with artificial intelligence software and concerned about the side effects of data centers, they have become a major issue in this year’s midterm elections. Alaska’s gubernatorial race is no exception, particularly since the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority announced plans for a development that could include data centers in Southcentral Alaska.
All four candidates — Republicans Dave Bronson, Treg Taylor and Bernadette Wilson and the Democratic Kreiss-Tomkins — have staked out different policy positions before Alaskans vote this fall.
Data centers need reliable connections to the internet, cheap electricity and a cooling method. Currently, the North Slope is the most promising location for all three.
One $500 million proposal on the North Slope intends to burn local natural gas for power and use the natural cold air of the Arctic.
Another shipping-container-sized plan involves a gas-powered data center processing Bitcoin. ✂️
===
The Left Wing Echo Chamber
The Jukebox is here. Varro is the host. The theme is Decades.
Another Saturday Night – Decades
This Week in the War on Women will be here or here (the first queries by publishing group, the second by tag). If one doesn’t show you the new diary, try the other.
Muriel gave us two today. I haven’t had time to read either yet.
If anyone has a diary of theirs that they’d like promoted, please drop a comment (preferably with a link) in the previous night’s Shade. Hopefully the next Shade will include a promotional link for you.
Today is…*
*Attributions to WineRev refer to his entries in his History Corner diary. I didn’t use his material today, but I do often enough that he has a perpetual attribution in my Shades.
Birthdays
William Sellers (1824-1905) – American engineer and inventor (US standard screw thread), born in Upper Darby, Pennsylvania.
[if he hadn’t been born, we wouldn’t be screwed]
Karen Aabye (1904 -1982) – Danish journalist, author (Min bedstemor er jomfru (My Grandmother is a Virgin)), and WWII resistance fighter, born in Copenhagen, Denmark.
Danish writer. In the late 1930s, she worked as a journalist in Paris and London before she gained popularity with a number of historical novels in which strong-willed women were her main characters. Her works also include travel books and a collection of essays. ✂️ [Wikipedia]
Leon Jaworski (1905-1982) – American Watergate scandal special prosecutor, born in Waco, Texas.
Sir William Golding was a British novelist, poet, and playwright best known for his debut novel “Lord of the Flies”, published in 1954. Throughout his career, he wrote 12 fiction novels, three non-fiction works, and various collections.
Golding is most notable for winning the 1983 Nobel Prize in Literature, and was knighted only five years later for his contributions to literature in 1988. He was also a fellow of the Royal Society of Literature.
Golding attended Brasenose College, Oxford, as a science major before transferring to English for his final two years. After graduating in 1934, his book of poems was published by Macmillan & Co. He later became a schoolmaster teaching various subjects and served in the Royal Navy during World War II.
In 2008, Golding was ranked third on The Times’ list of 50 greatest British writers since 1945.
Frances Farmer (1913-1970) – American actress (Son of Fury, Flowing Gold, Among the Living), born in Seattle, Washington.
Jay Ward (1920-1989) – Cartoonist and illustrator who created The Adventures of Rocky and Bullwinkle and Friends.
(1:56)
Adam West [William West Anderson] (1928-2017) – American actor (Batman, Last Precinct), born in Walla Walla, Washington
(0:49)
After being discharged from the army, in part due to his homosexuality, and then pursuing training as an actor, Brian Epstein joined his family’s retail business, running their North End Music Store (known as NEMS). He expanded the inventory from pianos and radios to include records, while also writing a column in ‘Mersey Beat’ a local music magazine.
After a customer request for an early recording that the Beatles made backing Tony Sheridan in Germany, Epstein went to see the group perform. He immediately saw their potential and with no experience in the business, became their manager. He polished their image and secured a proper record contract. The success he had with the Beatles enabled him to expand his roster of clients to include other Liverpudlian acts: Gerry and the Pacemakers, Cilla Black, and Billy J. Kramer and The Dakotas.
Bra Willie [Keorapetse Kgositsile](1938-2018) – South African poet (When the Clouds Clear; My Name Is Afrika; Point of Departure), and political activist, born in Johannesburg, South Africa
“Mama” Cass gained fame as part of the 1960s folk-pop vocal quartet the Mamas & the Papas. The group was together from 1965 until 1968, before personal issues tore them apart. They released 4 albums and had 6 Top-Ten singles, including “California Dreamin’” and “Monday, Monday”.
“Dream A Little Dream of Me” recorded by the group, was released as a single giving Elliot top billing, and launching her solo career. Elliot would go on to released 4 studio albums and a live set, with her biggest hit being “Make Your Own Kind of Music”. A final group album was recorded in 1971 – mostly with individual parts overdubbed – to complete contract obligations.
After some ups and downs, and health and substance issues, Elliot settled into a nightclub and theater routine that was proving successful and fulfilling. After a two-week run at London’s Palladium, she died in her sleep of a heart attack at 32.
She was inducted in to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1998, and received a star on the Hollywood walk of Fame in 2022.
(Lawrence) “Lol” Creme (1947-Still Living) – English rock vocalist, songwriter, keyboardist, guitarist (10cc – “I’m Not On Love”, “The Things We Do for Love; Godley & Creme – “Cry”), and music video director, born in Prestwich, Lancashire, England
Daniel Lanois (1951-Still Living) – Canadian record producer (Brian Eno; U2; Peter Gabriel; Bob Dylan), and singer-songwriter, born in Hull, Quebec
Partial discography [via Wikipedia and kraigo]
The Unforgettable Fire – U2
So – Peter Gabriel
The Joshua Tree – U2
Oh Mercy – Bob Dylan
Yellow Moon – The Neville Brothers
Achtung Baby – U2
Us – Peter Gabriel
Wrecking Ball – Emmylou Harris
Teatro – Willie Nelson
All That You Can’t Leave Behind – U2
How to Dismantle An Atomic Bomb – U2
Back Where You Belong – Sinéad O’Connor
Battle Born – The Killers
Pink Elephant – Arcade Fire
===
Events
In 1796, President George Washington’s farewell address was published. In it, America’s first chief executive advised, “Observe good faith and justice toward all nations. Cultivate peace and harmony with all.”
In 1881, the 20th president of the United States, James A. Garfield, died 2 1/2 months after being shot by Charles Guiteau; he was succeeded by Vice President Chester A. Arthur.
In 1893 New Zealand becomes the first country to grant all women the right to vote.
(6:57)
In 1955, President Juan Peron of Argentina was ousted after a revolt by the army and navy.
In 1957, the United States conducted its first contained underground nuclear test, code-named “Rainier,” in the Nevada desert.
In 1985, the Mexico City area was struck by a devastating earthquake that killed at least 9,500 people.
In 1988, Olympic diver Greg Louganis suffered a concussion after striking his head on the diving board during the preliminary round of the 3-meter springboard diving competition at the Seoul Summer Games; Louganis would recover from the injury and win a gold medal in the event the following day.
In 1995, The New York Times and The Washington Post published the manifesto of Unabomber Ted Kaczynski (kah-ZIHN’-skee), which proved instrumental in identifying and capturing him.
[with AI, the Unibomber is being proven right. I’m not endorsing his actions, but the reasoning was sound]
In 2004, Hu Jintao (hoo jin-tow) became the undisputed leader of China with the departure of former President Jiang Zemin (jahng zuh-MEEN’) from his top military post.
In 2008, struggling to stave off financial catastrophe, the Bush administration laid out a radical bailout plan calling for a takeover of a half-trillion dollars or more in worthless mortgages and other bad debt held by tottering institutions. Relieved investors sent stocks soaring on Wall Street and around the globe.
In 2011, Mariano Rivera of the New York Yankees recorded his 602nd save, making him baseball’s all-time leader in the category.
In 2022, Great Britain and the world said a final goodbye to Queen Elizabeth II at a state funeral that drew presidents and kings, princes and prime ministers — and crowds who thronged the streets of London.
===
National Days
Yar harrr! Ahoy there ye lily livered blaggards! Talk Like a Pirate Day means it’s time for pillaging and the imbibing of rum!
Pirates have been all the rage in recent years, and out of that particular fascination came an insane and completely pirate-oriented idea: that there should be a day dedicated to keeping the piratical language alive and, more importantly, the tradition of all things related to pirates.
So Talk Like a Pirate Day was invented. And now it’s time to celebrate with all of the pirate talk that can be mustered in one day!
=
Software Freedom Day is all about giving people the keys to their own digital world. It celebrates software that anyone can use, share, or change—no locked doors, no hidden rules.
On this day, folks from all walks of life come together to talk about how tech can stay fair and open. It’s not just for programmers; it’s for parents, students, workers—anyone who’s ever clicked a mouse or tapped a screen.
In friendly gatherings around the world, people trade stories, try out new tools, and help each other understand what “free software” really means. Some discover apps that can replace expensive programs.
Others get inspired to join global projects where their ideas actually matter. Everyone walks away knowing more and feeling more in control.
That’s the real magic—turning complex code into something simple, helpful, and truly shared.
=
As National Dance Day approaches, dance studios and activewear brands typically roll out exciting promotions. In 2026, expect special class rates from local studios like Arthur Murray Dance Centers and Fred Astaire Dance Studios, encouraging new sign-ups. Retailers such as Capezio and Bloch often offer discounts on dancewear and shoes. Fitness apps like Steezy Studio may feature free trial periods or reduced subscription costs for their online classes. Even entertainment venues might host special dance nights or themed events. We will update this page with confirmed live deals as September 19 approaches.
=
Batman Day swoops into action every third Saturday in September, uniting fans worldwide to honor the iconic Caped Crusader. Dive into Gotham’s world through classic comics, blockbuster films, and thrilling animated series. Join the global celebration by dressing up, re-reading your favorite stories, and sharing your love for the Dark Knight.
I still think this one was the best (1:47)
===
Tomorrow Is…
Smooch ’em if you’ve got ’em.
For Lol Creme’s birthday (4:02)
Welcome to the Caturday Evening Post.

item.title: [fansided.com] MLB playoff picture: Updated standings, postseason matchups and teams still alive
item.dc:creator: Jake Elman
item.description: Those following the Major League Baseball postseason picture will see and hear the term “earn” frequently mentioned within the coming days, which isn’t exactly the word that comes to mind upon looking at the standings. Outside of the 60-game 2020 season, we’ve never seen a losing team make the playoffs. Depending on how the next eight days play out, there could be four American League teams that finish with 81 or fewer wins yet qualify for the playoffs. The easiest way to keep tabs on how close
item.content:encoded:
Those following the Major League Baseball postseason picture will see and hear the term “earn” frequently mentioned within the coming days, which isn’t exactly the word that comes to mind upon looking at the standings.
Outside of the 60-game 2020 season, we’ve never seen a losing team make the playoffs. Depending on how the next eight days play out, there could be four American League teams that finish with 81 or fewer wins yet qualify for the playoffs.
The easiest way to keep tabs on how close teams are to clinching is by looking at magic numbers. The formula to calculate a magic number is as follows, per MLB.com:
- Games remaining +1 - (Losses by second place team - losses by first place team)
American League standings and playoff picture
For all intents and purposes, the Red Sox have clinched a playoff berth; they entered Saturday with their magic number sitting at two, and they’re so far ahead in the Wild Card standings that they’re all but locked into a first-round matchup with the Yankees. It’d be the fourth time in less than a decade these two have met in the playoffs, and the Red Sox look to avenge last year’s Wild Card Series loss.
The AL Central and AL West are, shall we say, messy. Houston holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over Texas and is only two games back of Cleveland for the AL’s No. 2 seed. Meanwhile, the White Sox have a one-game lead over the Rangers for the final Wild Card berth, and we could realistically see three of those teams make the postseason with a losing record.
| Team | Record | Games back |
|---|---|---|
| Tampa Bay Rays | 93-60 | -- |
| Cleveland Guardians | 79-75 | 14.5 |
| Houston Astros | 77-77 | 16.5 |
| New York Yankees | 89-64 (WC) | 4 |
| Boston Red Sox | 84-70 (WC) | 9.5 |
| Chicago White Sox | 78-76 (WC) | 15.5 |
| Texas Rangers | 77-77 (OUT) | 16.5 |
| Toronto Blue Jays | 76-78 (OUT) | 16.5 |
| Baltimore Orioles | 75-79 (OUT) | 18.5 |
If the regular season ended today, here's a look at what the AL Wild Card round matchups would look like.
- Bye: (1) Tampa Bay Rays
- Bye: (2) Cleveland Guardians
- (3) Houston Astros vs. (6) Chicago White Sox
- (4) New York Yankees vs. (5) Boston Red Sox
National League standings and playoff picture
The only thing that’s changed in the National League is how crowded the Wild Card race has become. Barring a collapse over the season’s final week, we’re all but assured of the Cubs, Phillies, and Padres being the three Wild Card teams. That’s been the case for most of September, as has the Braves being the No. 3 seed and NL East champions.
How the seeding will work, though, is where things get interesting. The Cubs, Phillies, and Padres all began Saturday at 85-69, and they’d be seeded in that order; No. 4 Chicago would host No. 5 Philadelphia, and No. 6 San Diego would play at Atlanta.
Unfortunately for the Phillies, they close the regular season with a six-game homestand against the Brewers and Rays. Both teams are still fighting for the top seeds in their respective leagues, so don’t expect them to go lightly on Don Mattingly’s club.
| Team | Record | Games back |
|---|---|---|
| Milwaukee Brewers | 93-60 | -- |
| Los Angeles Dodgers | 79-75 | 2.0 |
| Atlanta Braves | 77-77 | 6.0 |
| Chicago Cubs | 85-69 (WC) | 11.0 |
| Philadelphia Phillies | 85-69 (WC) | 11.0 |
| San Diego Padres | 85-69 (WC) | 11.0 |
| Arizona Diamondbacks | 80-74 (OUT) | 16.0 |
If the regular season ended today, here’s a look at what the NL Wild Card round matchups would look like.
- Bye: (1) Milwaukee Brewers
- Bye: (2) Los Angeles Dodgers
- (3) Atlanta Braves vs. (6) San Diego Padres
- (4) Chicago Cubs vs. (5) Philadelphia Phillies
MLB magic numbers: Which AL teams are closest to clinching a playoff spot?
| Team | Magic number | Elimination number |
|---|---|---|
| Tampa Bay Rays | CLINCHED | -- |
| Cleveland Guardians | 7 | -- |
| Houston Astros | 8 | -- |
| New York Yankees | CLINCHED | -- |
| Boston Red Sox | 2 | -- |
| Chicago White Sox | 7 | 8 |
| Texas Rangers | | 8 |
| Toronto Blue Jays | | 6 |
| Baltimore Orioles | | 6 |
| Detroit Tigers | | 3 |
| Seattle Mariners | | 4 |
| Minnesota Twins | | 3 |
| Kansas City Royals | -- | ELIMINATED |
| Athletics | -- | ELIMINATED |
| Los Angeles Angels | -- | ELIMINATED |
As we said, half of the AL playoff picture has essentially already been determined. Only three games separate the White Sox and Orioles, who are still mathematically alive despite entering Saturday with a 75-79 record. Let’s also not forget about the 76-78 Blue Jays, who are only two games back of the White Sox.
We recently referenced the 2008 Yankees, who missed the playoffs at 89-73 and watched the Dodgers win the NL West with 84 wins. If we created a portal and grabbed that Yankees team, they’d be the AL’s No. 4 seed if the playoffs began tomorrow, and it wouldn’t be close. Great job, all.
But hey, we objectively love chaos, so we’re in the minority in loving the AL playoff picture.
MLB magic numbers: Which NL teams are closest to clinching a playoff spot?
There’s not much else to say about the National League playoff picture. The teams that haven’t officially locked up a playoff berth should do so within the coming days, and the Diamondbacks’ tragic number dropped to four following Friday night’s loss to the Yankees.
| Team | Magic number | Elimination number |
|---|---|---|
| Milwaukee Brewers | CLINCHED | -- |
| Los Angeles Dodgers | CLINCHED | -- |
| Atlanta Braves | CLINCHED | -- |
| Chicago Cubs | 3 | -- |
| Philadelphia Phillies | 4 | -- |
| San Diego Padres | 4 | -- |
| Arizona Diamondbacks | -- | 4 |
| Pittsburgh Pirates | -- | ELIMINATED |
| Miami Marlins | -- | ELIMINATED |
| St. Louis Cardinals | -- | ELIMINATED |
| Washington Nationals | -- | ELIMINATED |
| Cincinnati Reds | -- | ELIMINATED |
| New York Mets | -- | ELIMINATED |
| San Francisco Giants | -- | ELIMINATED |
| Colorado Rockies | -- | ELIMINATED |
It’s hard not to feel bad for the Rockies. Despite not blowing up their roster at the trade deadline, they're 13-31 since Aug. 1, and they haven't had a winning streak longer than four games all year. Warren Schaeffer’s club is two losses away from its fourth consecutive 100-loss season, and they’ve been outscored by nearly 200 runs.
But considering they went 43-119 last year, this technically means they’ve made significant progress. Yikes.

item.content:encoded:
Los New York Yankees respondieron con autoridad en su primer partido sin Aaron Judge y derrotaron 9-2 a los Arizona Diamondbacks este viernes en Chase Field. Nueva York fabricó cinco carreras en la primera entrada, Ben Rice y George Lombard Jr. conectaron cuadrangulares y Gerrit Cole lanzó seis entradas de calidad para llevarse una victoria que también tuvo un significado histórico para el derecho.
LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Aaron Judge vuelve a la lista de lesionados de los Yankees!
LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Dodgers ya son campeones de la División Oeste!
Suscríbete al Newsletter de Unanimo y recibe gratis las últimas noticias. Dale click aquí
La jornada comenzó con una noticia importante para los Yankees: Judge fue colocado nuevamente en la lista de lesionados de 10 días debido a una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha. Sin su principal figura ofensiva, Nueva York necesitó encontrar producción desde el primer turno y la respuesta llegó inmediatamente frente al abridor de Arizona, Eduardo Rodríguez.
Los primeros cinco bateadores de los Yankees lograron embasarse. Ben Rice recibió una base por bolas y posteriormente Amed Rosario conectó un sencillo productor para abrir la pizarra. Después llegaron más oportunidades para la ofensiva neoyorquina, hasta que George Lombard Jr. conectó un sencillo de dos carreras que llevó el marcador a 5-0 antes de que terminara el primer episodio. Rodríguez necesitó 45 lanzamientos para conseguir los tres outs de la entrada, la mayor cantidad de su carrera en un primer inning.
Arizona intentó reaccionar en el segundo capítulo. Corbin Carroll conectó un cuadrangular de dos carreras para acercar a los Diamondbacks a 5-2 y darle algo de vida al público de Chase Field. Sin embargo, Cole logró contener la ofensiva local y evitó que la reacción se transformara en una amenaza mayor.
La respuesta de los Yankees llegó en la tercera entrada. Ben Rice volvió a aparecer y conectó un cuadrangular solitario, su número 39 de la temporada, para recuperar la diferencia de cuatro carreras y colocar el encuentro 6-2. El batazo también completó una noche ofensiva sobresaliente para Rice, quien terminó con dos imparables, dos bases por bolas, dos carreras y dos carreras impulsadas.
Mientras la ofensiva seguía produciendo, Cole encontró estabilidad desde la lomita. Después del cuadrangular de Carroll, el derecho no permitió otra carrera y completó seis entradas con cuatro hits, dos carreras limpias, ninguna base por bolas y seis ponches. Venía de dos aperturas en las que había permitido siete jonrones combinados, por lo que su actuación en Phoenix representó una recuperación importante en su temporada.
Lombard Jr. volvió a aparecer en la sexta entrada. El campocorto conectó su tercer jonrón de la temporada, esta vez solitario, para ampliar la ventaja de Nueva York a 7-2. El joven infielder terminó la noche con dos imparables y tres carreras impulsadas, convirtiéndose en otra de las figuras ofensivas del triunfo visitante.
Ver esta publicación en Instagram
Los Yankees agregaron dos carreras más en la séptima entrada para terminar de sentenciar el encuentro. La ofensiva visitante terminó con ocho hits y nueve carreras, mientras que Arizona consiguió siete imparables, pero no volvió a pisar el plato después del segundo inning.
Para Cole, la victoria tuvo un valor especial. El derecho llegó a 162 triunfos en su carrera, superando a Mike Moore y convirtiéndose en el lanzador con más victorias entre los jugadores que fueron seleccionados con el primer pick global del Draft. Cole fue elegido por los Pittsburgh Pirates con la primera selección en 2011.
La derrota, en cambio, complicó todavía más el panorama de Arizona en la recta final de la temporada. Los Diamondbacks llegaron al encuentro buscando mantenerse en la pelea por el último boleto de comodín de la Liga Nacional, pero la caída ante Nueva York significó su tercera derrota consecutiva. Al término de la jornada quedaron cinco juegos por detrás del último puesto de Wild Card, con ocho encuentros restantes.
Los Yankees, ya clasificados a los playoffs, mejoraron a 89-64 y se colocaron a cuatro juegos de los Tampa Bay Rays en la División Este de la Liga Americana, con nueve partidos por disputar. Nueva York además consiguió su octava victoria en sus últimos 10 encuentros.
El triunfo llegó, además, en una noche en la que los Yankees tuvieron que afrontar la ausencia de Judge. Rice y Lombard Jr. aportaron los batazos largos, mientras que Cole respondió desde el montículo para que Nueva York tomara el primer partido de la serie en Arizona con una victoria contundente de 9-2.

item.content:encoded:
Redacción FOX Deportes
Aaron Judge confía en que podrá volver en los playoffs
El jardinero y cañonero de los Yankees fue colocado en la lista de lesionados
Después de ser enviado a la lista de lesionados por diez días debido a una distensión en el músculo sóleo derecho, Aaron Judge expresó su deseo de regresar para los playoffs.
“Me gustaría estar de vuelta para la postemporada; ese es definitivamente el plan”, declaró el capitán de los Yankees. El jardinero confirmó que mantendrá sus rutinas de tiro y entrenamiento físico “para volver de inmediato en cuanto estemos listos” y afrontar el cierre del campeonato.
Respecto a la gravedad de la lesión, el estelar bateador admitió que la localización de la molestia ha dificultado su movilidad en el terreno. “He lidiado con distensiones antes y he jugado así, pero esto fue en un lugar diferente que lo hizo un poco más difícil”, explicó Judge, añadiendo que el sóleo “es más crucial para correr y batear”. Sobre su tiempo de baja, reconoció que no tiene certeza: “El cuerpo médico no me ha dicho el grado aún y no tengo respuestas sobre plazos”.
Los Yankees colocaron a Aaron Judge en la lista de lesionados
El equipo neoyorquino se quedará sin su máxima estrella en la parte final de la temporada
Por su parte, el mánager Aaron Boone adoptó una postura pragmática y evitó ofrecer un diagnóstico médico o una fecha estimada para el retorno de su figura. “No importa qué grado sea, nos quedan nueve partidos”, afirmó el estratega ante los medios de comunicación. “Vamos a trabajar para tenerlo de regreso o no; eso es lo que vamos a hacer y ya veremos qué sucede”, enfatizó sobre las posibilidades de volver a contar con el jugador en el roster.
La fecha más cercana para la reactivación de Judge es el 29 de septiembre frente a los Orioles, día en que también inicia la Serie de Comodines de la Liga Americana. El vigente Jugador Más Valioso busca reincorporarse a tiempo para los playoffs tras una campaña afectada por los problemas físicos, en la que registra un promedio de .241 con 18 cuadrangulares y 41 carreras impulsadas en 66 partidos disputados esta temporada.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees at Diamondbacks. Cam Schlittler dominating in early innings
The Yankees broke through with the first run of the game in the top of the fifth inning, while the Diamondbacks are still looking for their first hit off Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler.
The Diamondbacks trail the Yankees, 1-0, after 4½ innings as play continued at Chase Field on Saturday, Sept. 19.
The Yankees loaded the bases on three singles in the fifth off right-hander Brandon Pfaadt, prompting manager Torey Lovullo to make an aggressive move to his bullpen. Right-hander Justin Martinez entered and recorded two fly-ball outs, the first of which, by Ben Rice, was deep enough to score the first run of the night.
The Diamondbacks are trying to keep their slim playoff hopes alive with a win. Meanwhile, the San Diego Padres, whom the Diamondbacks are hoping to catch, were losing to the Marlins at Petco Park.
The game started about a half-hour late after a lengthy pregame ceremony honoring the Diamondbacks’ 2001 World Series team.
With former radio voice Greg Schulte hosting the ceremony, the Diamondbacks introduced players, coaches and staff from the ‘01 team. Randy Johnson was the last one announced. While everyone else entered the field from beyond the right-field fence, Johnson came out of the home bullpen in left field, a call back to his relief appearance in Game 7 of the World Series.
One of the memorable moments of the pregame ceremony was when trumpeter Dr. Jesse McGuire, performing the national anthem as he did at the World Series in 2001, hit a sour note on his instrument. Then the trumpet gave out completely, and McGuire acted quickly by grabbing the microphone and singing the rest of the Star-Spangled Banner.
Afterward, he received a hug from Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo as the crowd cheered.
—Nick Piercoro and Jose M. Romero
With his team teetering on the brink of elimination, Lovullo’s job status is again a topic of discussion. Lovullo understands. For him, it’s nothing new.
“It seems to be a very important part of the conversation for a lot of people,” Lovullo said on Saturday, Sept. 19, a day after his team lost for the third consecutive day to drop five games out of a playoff spot with eight games remaining.
“For me, it’s real, I understand it, but it’s the realities of this game. You’ve got to win. That’s what it comes down to. Have we won enough? You know, I want to win every game that we play.”
Lovullo, in his 10th season as Diamondbacks manager, has worked as a “lame-duck” manager in four of the past six seasons. He seemed to reference that history, as well as the fact that he had to “fight for everything” during his playing career.
But he said that, for now, at least, he remains focused on doing what he can to help his players and coaches finish out the season.
“When it’s time to worry about it or think about it, whether that’s sooner than later, I will,” he said. “I’ve got to do my job. If I'm worried about different things that I can’t control, then I'm not doing my job for that group in there. I’m doing fine. I’m doing fine. Because I've lived in this space for a long time. I understand the playbook. I understand the realities of this game.”
Last year, Lovullo went into the final weekend of the year with similar questions surrounding him. He found out a day after the season ended that he would be coming back for another year.
The situation is believed to be similar to then: Lovullo has strong support from the baseball operations department and general manager Mike Hazen, but how he is viewed by ownership is less certain.
Lovullo has two postseason appearances — 2017 and 2023 — during his managerial tenure, but he also has presided over multiple late-season collapses. If this year's team continues to stumble, it would mark a third consecutive year the Diamondbacks fell short in September.
Hazen is working under the five-year extension he signed in September 2023. His deal runs through 2028.
The Diamondbacks entered Saturday, Sept. 19, facing long odds at a postseason berth. FanGraphs put their chances at claiming a wild-card spot at about 5%.
—Nick Piecoro
Justin Martinez leaves impression on manager
Members of the 2001 Diamondbacks World Series team milled about in front of the home dugout at Chase Field on Friday, Sept. 18, catching up, taking photos and conducting interviews.
Justin Martinez walked among them, asking each one he approached to sign a baseball. The Diamondbacks reliever later put the ball in a case he had with him in the team clubhouse.
Lovullo said Martinez seeking autographs of veterans is a throwback to a previous generation of players.
“I love it,” Lovullo said. “There was probably seven fistfights between those teammates, firstfights don’t happen anymore. It’s just a different level of camaraderie. But players care about the same thing, and that’s to win the world championship.
“So ‘J-Mart’ was probably just getting a feel for the common denominator based on what drove that team, and that’s a brotherhood that you can’t replace.”
Lovullo added that he's happy that the current team has players that are fans of baseball on that level.
“That he gets to touch their emotions makes it even better. That’s vintage J-Mart," Lovullo said.
— José M. Romero
Yankees at Diamondbacks, 5:10 p.m., Cox, Ch. 34
Diamondbacks RHP Brandon Pfaadt (7-3, 3.77) vs. Yankees RHP Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95).
At Chase Field: Pfaadt gave up six runs in 6⅔ innings against the Rangers in his most recent start. All six runs came in the fifth inning, in which Pfaadt was ruled to have missed the bag while covering first, opening the door for the final four runs of the inning to score. … Pfaadt has had a strong past few months overall, but his past five starts have been rough. He has posted a 5.74 ERA in 31⅓ innings in that stretch. … He has faced the Yankees only once in his career, giving up six runs (five earned) in 4⅓ innings in a game in 2023. … Schlittler looks like the favorite to win the American League Cy Young Award. He has the lowest ERA and WHIP and has logged 184⅔. … He has never faced the Diamondbacks. … Schlittler averages 98 mph with his four-seam fastball. He primarily throws that, his sinker and cutter, only occasionally sprinkling in curveballs and a rare slider.
Coming up
Sunday, Sept. 20: At Chase Field, 1:10 p.m., Diamondbacks RHP Corbin Burnes (0-0, 5.87) vs. Yankees RHP Will Warren (10-6, 3.89).
Monday, Sept. 21: Off.
Tuesday, Sept. 22: At Colorado, 5:40 p.m., Diamondbacks RHP Michael Soroka (8-5, 3.45) vs. Rockies LHP Kyle Freeland (4-10, 6.38).
Wednesday, Sept. 23: At Colorado, 5:40 p.m., Diamondbacks RHP Merrill Kelly (9-14, 5.00) vs. Rockies RHP Mason Adams (0-1, 5.09).

Aaron Judge recibió un nuevo golpe en una temporada marcada por las lesiones. El capitán de los New York Yankees regresó a la lista de lesionados debido a una distensión muscular en la pantorrilla derecha, situación que genera incertidumbre sobre su participación en el cierre de la campaña y en los Playoffs de las Grandes Ligas. El mánager Aaron Boone confir
item.content:encoded:
¡Alerta en los Yankees! Aaron Judge regresa a la lista de lesionados
Aaron Boone reconoció que todavía no existe una fecha para su regreso.
Aaron Judge recibió un nuevo golpe en una temporada marcada por las lesiones. El capitán de los New York Yankees regresó a la lista de lesionados debido a una distensión muscular en la pantorrilla derecha, situación que genera incertidumbre sobre su participación en el cierre de la campaña y en los Playoffs de las Grandes Ligas.
El mánager Aaron Boone confirmó que el equipo todavía no cuenta con un calendario definido para la recuperación del bateador.
“No tengo un plazo definido para su recuperación”, dijo el piloto, quien tampoco pudo garantizar la presencia de Judge en la postemporada. Ante la pregunta sobre si estará disponible para los Playoffs, su respuesta fue contundente: “No lo sé”.
Judge apenas había regresado el 8 de septiembre, después de perder tiempo por una fractura en la costilla derecha. En seis encuentros desde su vuelta, registró cuatro imparables en 23 turnos, además de un cuadrangular, para un promedio de .174.
El problema físico apareció durante el duelo del miércoles ante los Mellizos de Minnesota. Judge abandonó el encuentro por molestias en la pierna derecha.
“Intenté restarle importancia y ver cuánto tiempo podía aguantar, porque estos partidos son importantes en la recta final de la temporada”, explicó Judge. “Pero, tras analizarlo, pensé que lo correcto era salir del juego para no perjudicar al equipo en el campo ni en las bases”.
Los Yankees, que buscan asegurar su lugar en la Postemporada. La temporada regular concluirá el 28 de septiembre, mientras que la Serie de Comodines de la Liga Americana comenzará el 29.

Now, they're once again back in action on Saturday evening with right-handed ace and AL Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler on the mound for the Yankees, while the Diamondbacks will have righty Brandon Pfaadt pitching. item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees secured a 9-2 series-opening victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday night.
Now, they're once again back in action on Saturday evening with right-handed ace and AL Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler on the mound for the Yankees, while the Diamondbacks will have righty Brandon Pfaadt pitching.
Ahead of the matchup, manager Aaron Boone didn't make any major changes to his starting lineup, but he did make some notable changes to his batting order.
Yankees Announce George Lombard Jr. Move
With outfielder Spencer Jones getting the day off and veteran Paul Goldschmidt out of the lineup after leading off on Friday, rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. is moving up in the batting order.
After hitting seventh in the series opener, Boone is placing Lombard Jr. in the five-hole Saturday, while Heliot Ramos bats cleanup and Ben Rice moves back into the leadoff role.
Cody Bellinger and Luis Garcia Jr. will remain in their normal roles, hitting second and third.
Here's the full Yankees lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: "Yankees 9/19 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF L. García Jr. 1B H. Ramos RF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B R. McMahon 3B J. Caballero CF C. Schlittler SP."
Yankees 9/19
B. Rice DH
C. Bellinger LF
L. García Jr. 1B
H. Ramos RF
G. Lombard Jr. SS
A. Wells C
A. Volpe 2B
R. McMahon 3B
J. Caballero CF
C. Schlittler SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 19, 2026
Lombard Jr.'s 2026 Season
Since the Yankees called him up on Aug. 4, Lombard Jr. has exceeded expectations and made an immediate impact for New York.
He's appeared in 35 games and has gone 29-for-124 with 19 runs, four home runs, and 15 RBIs while hitting .234 with a .371 slugging percentage and a .663 OPS.
Looking at the Yankees
New York enters Saturday with an 89-64 overall record and currently holds the top Wild Card spot, which would set them up to host a Wild Card series at home in the Bronx.
That said, they're just 4.0 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the AL East and the No. 1 overall seed in the AL, with an upcoming four-game set against the Rays this week.

The rookie outfielder claimed it was “no big deal” and chalked it up to the wear and tear of playing on Chase Field’s turf Friday night after jamming his heel in Minnesota earlier this week.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — In case the Yankees weren’t dealing with enough injury headaches for a 6-foot-7 slugger, Spencer Jones was out of the lineup Saturday with a sore left foot/heel.
The rookie outfielder claimed it was “no big deal” and chalked it up to the wear and tear of playing on Chase Field’s turf Friday night after jamming his heel in Minnesota earlier this week.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
But after the Yankees just lost Aaron Judge to the injured list again with a right calf strain, the last thing they needed was Jones nursing an injury of his own.
“Just a little banged up,” Jones said before Saturday’s game against the Diamondbacks. “Playing on turf is different, hard on the feet.”
Aaron Boone also downplayed it, adding that he still almost kept Jones in the lineup before sitting him in favor of José Caballero, who started in center field for the second time this season.
“Just felt like especially being on the turf here, he kind of jammed that heel in Minnesota and being on the turf [Friday], so I think it’s just a day-to-day kind of thing,” Boone said. “I even view him as available tonight.”
Boone said he preferred to keep Cody Bellinger in left field instead of shifting him to center.
“I considered moving him to center, but Belli’s grinding too and the turf here kind of beats you up,” he said. “There’s some scenarios where I would move him to center. Tonight, just being on the turf and as much as he’s been through this year, I didn’t want to move him.”
When the Yankees officially placed Judge on the 10-day injured list Saturday, they opted for defensive versatility over offensive upside in his replacement.
That meant calling up Max Schuemann instead of Jasson Domínguez, giving the former another shot in the big leagues for at least a few days beginning this weekend against the Diamondbacks.
“Adding his versatility to our bench makes some sense,” Boone said. “And then obviously some different roster complications moving forward with the playoffs around the corner.”
Schuemann’s stay may be brief, with Jazz Chisholm Jr. potentially returning from the IL as soon as the upcoming series against the Rays at Yankee Stadium that begins Tuesday.
If Schuemann goes back to Triple-A to make room, he would not be available to be recalled for 10 days (unless he was replacing an injured player again), essentially ruling him out as an option for the AL wild-card series.
That may have played a part in Domínguez not getting the call this time, in case the Yankees wanted to use him as a pinch-running threat on their playoff roster.
The 23-year-old also offers value as a switch-hitter, but he has proven to be a defensive liability in the outfield.
The Yankees’ trip to Chase Field gave them a chance to reunite with former teammate Jonathan Loáisiga, who has finally stayed healthy for a full season in the Diamondbacks bullpen.
Shop Yankees Merch
The right-hander often flashed his talent during his eight-year tenure with the Yankees, but injuries too often got in the way.
This season, though, after signing a minor league deal with the Diamondbacks, Loáisiga has avoided the IL and pitched in a career-high 64 games with a 2.32 ERA entering Saturday.
“Been through a lot of battles over the years with Jonny,” Boone said. “It’ll be great to see him. Hopefully we can ding him a little bit here. I know he’s had a really strong year, which I’m excited about for him. He’s such a talented guy that for him, it’s always been about just being healthy. So the fact that he’s gone out there and had a largely healthy season, I’m not surprised at the success he’s had.”
The Diamondbacks held a 25th-anniversary celebration Saturday of their 2001 World Series team that beat the Yankees in seven games.

item.title: [New York Daily News] Aaron Judge, Yankees claim they know nothing about severity of superstar’s calf strain

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — The Yankees continued to treat Aaron Judge’s calf strain like classified CIA intel on Saturday, as neither the back-to-back MVP nor Aaron Boone shared a grade for the injury.
Actually, both claimed that they don’t even know the answer to that question before the Bombers played the Diamondbacks.
“I gotta talk to the trainers and figure that out,” Judge said when asked for the grade after officially going on the 10-day injured list. “They got all the reports on that.”
Wait, the Yankees’ training staff hasn’t told Judge the grade of his strain?
“They haven’t told me yet,” said the captain, who is only seven games removed from a 99-day absence for a fractured rib that he approvingly skipped a rehab assignment for.
Okay, but surely the trainers told Boone, right?
Wrong, said the manager, as Boone stated that he hasn’t bothered to ask for the grade.
“It doesn’t matter what grade it is,” Boone said. “We’re at nine games left [in the season].
“If and when he’s able to be back, he will.”
It doesn’t matter? The Boston Sports Medicine & Research Institute begs to differ, stating a first-degree, or mild, calf strain comes with a 1-3-week timeline. A second-degree, or moderate, strain requires 3-6 weeks of rest and recovery before returning to full activity. A third-degree, or severe, strain “can take many weeks or months to fully heal.”
The severity of Judge’s injury is important because the second-place Yankees’ postseason will begin with the Wild Card round on Sept. 29 if the current standings hold. Judge is obviously instrumental to their chances of fulfilling their championship goals, but it is unclear if he’ll be back in time for the Wild Card round or any postseason action.
“I’d like to be back by the postseason. That’s definitely the plan,” said Judge, noting that the earliest he can return is the last game of the regular season. “So we’ll see. I got really no answers for you on any timeline or anything like that.”
Judge, who is continuing to throw, work out and get treatment, added that he’s “gonna do everything we can to get back as soon as we can.” Boone, meanwhile, said that he wouldn’t speculate on Judge’s timeline, but he’s “hoping for the best.”
“We’re gonna get him back or we’re not,” the skipper said. “That’s what we’re gonna work to do, and we’ll see.”
It is no surprise that the Yankees have not revealed many details since Judge hurt his calf in the first frame of Wednesday’s loss to the Twins, a game he did not exit until the sixth inning.
Judge has been notoriously withholding when talking about his various injuries over the years, and he prefers that the Yankees follow suit. They tend to oblige; Boone used the phrase “I don’t know” eight times while discussing Judge’s calf strain before Friday’s game.
The Yankees typically provide a grade within a day or two when a player suffers a strain.
One detail that Judge did share is that he strained the soleus muscle in his calf, as opposed to the gastrocnemius muscle. Judge’s understanding is that the soleus muscle is more “crucial” to running and hitting.
He also said that he “usually” deals with “calf stuff all year long,” but it doesn’t become public, and he doesn’t miss games.
It had been his hope that history would repeat itself, but a return to the injured list couldn’t be avoided this time around.
“I’m definitely frustrated,” said Judge, who has only played in 66 games this season. “I’ve dealt with strains before and kind of played through them, but this was kind of in a different spot where it made it a little bit more difficult.
“The focus is still the same: to get ready to go for October.”

item.content:encoded:
Last night was a good night for the Yankees, seeing the team put up five runs in the first paired with a good Gerrit Cole outing to cruise to a 9-2 win over the Diamondbacks. The club also picked up a game on the Rays as the AL East leaders dropped the opener of their series to the Red Sox. Tonight, the Yankees have two goals: get the win to stay in a hypothetically-competitive division race (all but necessary since Tampa Bay avenged the loss with a 2-1 win over Boston this afternoon), and build out a little more breathing room in the Cy Young race.
Dylan Cease had his worst start of the year on Friday for the Blue Jays, going just 2.2 innings and walking six. He and today's Yankee starter Cam Schlittler have had a heavyweight bout atop the Cy leaderboard all year, and while Cam's pulled away a bit in recent weeks, he can start to put the finishing touches on his case tonight. He hasn't allowed more than one earned run in a start since August 3rd (!!), making us all maybe expect a bit too much from the righty who can seemingly do no wrong. Schlittler has thrown 45 innings across those aforementioned seven starts, so he's not a five-and-fly guy, and his 1.00 ERA in that stretch is just…a farce.
Brandon Pfaadt is having the best season of his young career, with a 3.77 ERA and 4.06 FIP that are both significant steps forward after a pretty lost 2025. He doesn't strike many men out though, and a 45 percent ground ball rate means heavy sinking fastballs in the zone. There will be pitches to hit from Pfaadt; you just need to be able to elevate them.
Ben Rice had himself a fantastic game cleaning up last night and is bumped up to the leadoff spot tonight, with
Luis García Jr. getting the nod over Paul Goldschmidt at first base. Spencer Jones reportedly has a sore left foot, which means we get José Caballero in center, and I'm going to withhold comment on that decision for now.
It's an 8:10pm Eastern start but not a national broadcast, this one's on YES. The Diamondbacks will be celebrating their 2001 World Series championship throughout the evening, which seems kind of lame because you can't really "win" a championship when you didn't have an opponent.

item.content:encoded:
The Yankees are already dealing with the loss of Aaron Judge, and now they have another outfielder on the MLB roster who is temporarily unavailable. Spencer Jones, one of New York’s biggest breakout stories over the past month, is out of Saturday’s lineup against the Arizona Diamondbacks with left foot soreness.
The rookie told MLB.com’s Bryan Hoch that he expects it to be a one-day issue, which should provide some relief for a Yankees team that cannot afford another significant injury.
Spencer Jones has become a key part of Yankees’ lineup
Jones’ emergence has been one of the more encouraging developments for New York this season. After struggling early in his rookie campaign, the 25-year-old has started to find his footing at the plate and has become the Yankees’ everyday center fielder.
Through his first 80 games, Jones is hitting .248/.318/.433 with 10 home runs and a 109 wRC+. More importantly, his September has been particularly impressive. He entered Saturday batting .340/.415/.532 with two homers, 12 RBIs and seven runs through his first 13 games of the month.
The Yankees have also been encouraged by the adjustments Jones has made against Major League pitching. Manager Aaron Boone previously compared his developmental path to Judge’s, noting that Jones’ enormous 6-foot-7 frame could become a major advantage as his adjustments continue to translate.
That makes Saturday’s lineup change particularly notable.
Yankees cannot afford another outfield injury
Jones is being held out as a precaution, with José Caballero taking over in center field Saturday. Jones has indicated that he expects to return Sunday, so there is currently no indication that the foot issue is expected to become a lengthy absence.
Still, the timing is less than ideal.
Judge officially returned to the injured list Saturday with a right calf strain and has no established timetable for his return. The Yankees recalled Max Schuemann to fill his roster spot, while the club is expected to rely more heavily on its remaining outfield options.
New York has already dealt with significant injuries across its roster this season. With the postseason approaching, the Yankees need Jones healthy and available because his recent production has given the lineup another legitimate offensive option.
For now, the hope is that Jones’ absence truly is nothing more than a one-day precaution.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees posted their starting lineup Saturday afternoon for the second game of a three-game set against the Arizona Diamondbacks, and Paul Goldschmidt was not in it.
New York is trying to take the series after a 9-2 win Friday night at Chase Field. Goldschmidt led off that game and finished with a hit, a walk and two runs scored.
The announced order put Ben Rice at designated hitter, Cody Bellinger in left field and Luis García Jr. at first base. Heliot Ramos started in right, George Lombard Jr. at shortstop, Austin Wells behind the plate, Anthony Volpe at second, Ryan McMahon at third and José Caballero in center. Cam Schlittler was listed as the starting pitcher.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Yankees 9/19 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF L. García Jr. 1B H. Ramos RF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B R. McMahon 3B J. Caballero CF C. Schlittler SP.”
Goldschmidt, a seven-time All-Star, is in his second season with the Yankees after signing a one-year deal in February. He entered Saturday hitting .253 with 85 hits, 18 home runs, 50 RBIs, 44 runs and one stolen base in 102 games.
The 39-year-old first baseman spent his first eight big-league seasons in Arizona. He made six straight All-Star teams from 2013 through 2018 while wearing a Diamondbacks uniform.
After leaving Phoenix, Goldschmidt spent six years with the St. Louis Cardinals and won National League Most Valuable Player honors in 2022.
The Yankees sit second in the American League East at 89-64 through 153 games. They have gone 8-2 in their last 10 and trail the Tampa Bay Rays by four games.
Arizona is third in the National League West at 80-74 after 154 games and 4-6 over its last 10.
Manager Aaron Boone has mixed Goldschmidt’s playing time throughout the second half as younger options such as Rice have taken on larger roles. Goldschmidt started Friday after sitting in recent games.
The veteran remains a respected presence in the clubhouse. The Yankees nominated him for the 2026 MLBPAA Heart and Hustle Award earlier this season.
Goldschmidt signed a one-year, $4 million contract with New York this past offseason after hitting .274 with 10 homers and 45 RBIs in 146 games during his first Yankees season.
He has 390 career home runs and 1,282 RBIs across 16 major-league seasons. Career numbers also include a .286 batting average and seven All-Star selections.
Saturday’s game was scheduled for late afternoon local time. A New York win would give the Yankees the series with one game left.
The Diamondbacks have struggled to find consistent production at first base this year after Goldschmidt left the organization years earlier.
New York continues to chase a postseason berth in the final weeks of the regular season. Goldschmidt’s availability as a pinch-hitter or late-inning option remains part of the roster mix even when he does not start.
The lineup change was posted hours before first pitch and immediately circulated among fans tracking the club’s late-season decisions.

Gerrit Cole got the start.
He allowed two earned runs in 6.0 innings (with six strikeouts).
Yankees Star Cole Makes Rice Statement
After the game, Cole was asked about Ben Rice (via YES Network).
Rice had two hits, including one home run and two walks.
Meredith Marakovits: “And Rice now, 39 home runs in the season. Just what have you thought of his production and what he has meant to this team?”
Cole: “Special, special year. Has made some really good adjustments from previous years going into this year. And I think he’s really started to kind of heat back up here the last few weeks after having to make some adjustments in the middle of the season. So not only is he really proficient with the bat, but he’s a smart player and a hard worker, which is leading him to have just a really outstanding season for us.”
Looking At Rice
Rice is in the middle of his third season at the MLB level (all with the Yankees).
He was picked in the 12th round of the 2021 MLB Draft.
Right now, Rice is batting .264 with 144 hits, 39 home runs, 94 RBIs, 100 runs and three stolen bases in 146 games.
Looking At Cole
Cole is in the middle of his 6th season pitching for the Yankees.
He has also spent time with the Pittsburgh Pirates and Houston Astros.
Right now, Cole is 9-9 with a 3.63 ERA in 21 starts this year.
Looking At The Yankees Right Now
The Yankees (89-64) have two more games with the Diamondbacks before they return home to host the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday.
They are 4.0 games back of the Rays.

item.dc:creator: Greg Joyce
item.description: PHOENIX — Without any guarantees of it happening, Aaron Judge is holding out hope of returning from a calf strain in time for the playoffs. “I’d like to be back by the postseason; that’s definitely the plan,” Judge said Saturday afternoon. “We’re going to do everything we can to get back as soon as we can.” Access the Yankees beat like never before Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees. That was a
item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Without any guarantees of it happening, Aaron Judge is holding out hope of returning from a calf strain in time for the playoffs.
“I’d like to be back by the postseason; that’s definitely the plan,” Judge said Saturday afternoon. “We’re going to do everything we can to get back as soon as we can.”
Access the Yankees beat like never before
Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
That was a slightly less definitive statement than what Judge consistently said during the summer when he was trying to come back from a right rib stress fracture, which he did after three-plus months on Sept. 8.
But now the clock is ticking even louder, with Saturday marking 10 days away from Game 1 of the American League wild card series.
“Definitely frustrated,” said Judge, who played seven games after missing 84 on the IL with the rib injury. “Dealt with strains before and kind of played through them, but this was in a different spot where it made it a little bit more difficult.”
Judge did not reveal what grade the strain was, but said it involved his Soleus muscle, which he indicated was more important to running and hitting compared to the gastrocnemius muscle.
“The focus is still the same, to be ready to go for October,” Judge said.
In the meantime, the Yankees are banking on their summer without Judge paying off now that he is back on the IL.
“Lean on each other,” Cody Bellinger said. “The game itself is hard; if you add too much pressure on yourself, the game becomes even harder. So we really just have to play for each other, lean on each other, pass the baton, do your job and control what you can control.”
The Yankees did that on Friday night, racing out of the gates to score five runs in the first inning of a 9-2 win against the Diamondbacks, just hours after the team announced Judge was going on the 10-day injured list with a right calf strain.
But they also got off well at the beginning of June after Judge landed on the IL with a right rib stress fracture before their lineup became a black hole for an extended stretch during the summer. They had finally started to break out of it shortly before Judge got back on Sept. 8, but after having him back for seven games, they now find themselves in the same spot again, less than two weeks away from the start of the playoffs.
“We’ve played most of the year this way, and I feel like in a lot of cases, especially some of our key guys over the last few weeks have started to, especially offensively, get it going like we know they’re capable of,” manager Aaron Boone said.
During the 84-game span that Judge missed this summer, the Yankees ranked 26th in runs per game (4.06), 29th in batting average (.227), 27th in OPS (.681), and 29th in WRC+ (90).
But over the tail end of that stretch, and into Judge’s return, the Yankees started to hit more like they are capable of. That included the trade deadline addition of Luis García Jr., the emergence of rookie outfielder Spencer Jones, and Bellinger getting back on track after returning from his own hamstring injury in August.
Perhaps most importantly, it has coincided with the reemergence of Ben Rice. The lefty slugger was a game wrecker for the first two months of the season before Judge went down, then cooled off a bit during the summer (albeit with some good stretches along the way) before catching fire again over the last few weeks. Entering Saturday, over his last 22 games, Rice had hit .353 with a 1.037 OPS and five home runs, including his 39th of the season Friday night.
“Special year,” Gerrit Cole said. “Has made some really good adjustments from previous years, going into this year, and I think he’s really started to heat back up here the last few weeks after having to make some adjustments in the middle of the season. Not only is he really proficient with the bat, but he’s a smart player and a hard worker, which is leading him to have a really outstanding season for us.”
The Yankees need that to continue for however long Judge is out (and even if and when he returns) for them to play deep into October, though Rice isn’t looking at it as having to do any more — which got some hitters in trouble during the three-time AL MVP’s first absence.
“I would think that everyone just goes out there and stays within themselves, tries to put together quality at-bat after quality at-bat,” he said. “Pitching is always going to be doing their thing, like they have for us all year. So from an offensive standpoint, just do what we did [Friday]: go out and have a team at-bat, trust the guy behind you and keep the line moving.”
To Rice’s point, the Yankees have leaned on the strength of their pitching staff all season, but that was especially the case during Judge’s three months on the IL this summer, when they were able to scratch out enough wins in low-scoring games, with their pitchers keeping them in it almost every night.
New York Post may be compensated and/or receive an affiliate commission if you buy something through our links.
“We have a lot of confidence in here,” Cole said. “For the most part of the summer, we’ve been tested really, really hard and we responded, by and large, really, really well. We have a lot of perfectionists in here. We’re always striving to be perfect and trying to be the best. But the reality is we’ve had a lot of obstacles we’ve had to overcome and, by and large, we’ve played really well.”

"I'd like to be back by the postseason, so we'll see," Judge said. "That's definitely the plan. I got really no answers for you on any timeline or anything like that.'' Judge, who missed three months with a fractured rib, is eligible to come off the injured list for the regular-season
item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — New York Yankees slugger Aaron Judge, speaking for the first time since going on the injured list with a strained right calf, provided no timeline Saturday for when he could possibly return to the lineup.
"I'd like to be back by the postseason, so we'll see," Judge said. "That's definitely the plan. I got really no answers for you on any timeline or anything like that.''
Judge, who missed three months with a fractured rib, is eligible to come off the injured list for the regular-season finale on Sept. 27. He injured his calf in his first at-bat Wednesday playing against the Minnesota Twins. The injury is in the soleus muscle of the calf, which makes it difficult to participate in any baseball activities, he said, except throwing to keep his arm in shape.
"Definitely frustrated,'' Judge, the three-time MVP, said. "I've dealt with strains before, and kind of played through them, but this was kind of in a different spot where it made it a little bit more difficult. But definitely frustrated because, you know, the ultimate goal was to try to come back to get a couple of games before the postseason, so it changes it a little bit.''
While Judge opted to resume playing with the Yankees instead of having a traditional minor-league rehab stint after such a lengthy absence, he isn't second-guessing his decision, nor for coming out of Wednesday's game when he first felt his calf strain.
"You know, you feel things every single year,'' Judge said. "I usually deal with calf stuff all year long, and it usually gets to you, and usually don't miss any games. So that was kind of the same thing I was feeling.
"I was feeling it. I was working my way back, and then something kind of grabs you at a strange time. So if this would have happened in the rehab game, I would have been probably a little bit more pissed than I was now.
"So, it is what it is.''
The Yankees, who are in the No. 1 wild-card spot, are expected to host the Boston Red Sox in a best-of-three series beginning Sept. 29 in the wild-card round at Yankee Stadium. The winner would play the first-place Tampa Bay Rays in the Division Series.
Follow Nightengale on X: @Bnightengale
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Aaron Judge would 'like to be back by the postseason' but has no timeline for Yankees return

Now, we've seen enough of him, even if it's been in a couple of disjointed stints, to get a good idea of who he is at the major league level. The answer: pretty damn good. After struggling early, Jones has found his footing. A big reason for his ascendancy has been surprising. The Vanderbilt product has mashed left-handed pitching. He's now logged 51 plate appearances against lefties and has slashed an eye
item.content:encoded:
There were many questions the New York Yankees needed Spencer Jones to answer this season. Now, we've seen enough of him, even if it's been in a couple of disjointed stints, to get a good idea of who he is at the major league level.
The answer: pretty damn good. After struggling early, Jones has found his footing. A big reason for his ascendancy has been surprising. The Vanderbilt product has mashed left-handed pitching.
He's now logged 51 plate appearances against lefties and has slashed an eye-watering .435/.490/.761 following his homer off Minnesota Twins lefty specialist Taylor Rodgers on Sept. 15. It was the first dinger Rodgers gave up to a left-handed hitter over 133 plate appearances this season.
The sample size isn't huge, but it's relatively significant. For example, Ben Rice has 209 plate appearances against lefties out of his 622 plate appearances. For Jones, the 51 matchups against southpaws are a decent portion of his 255 total plate appearances.
One of the most impressive things about how he's performed against same-handed pitching is the amount of power he's demonstrated. Obviously, the six-foot-seven outfielder is a behemoth, but most lefties, even those who perform well against southpaws, see a drop in power in those situations. Take Rice, for instance; his slugging percentage drops from .561 against righties to .457 against left-handers. That hasn't been the case for Jones.
This has just been one part of Jones' maturation process that should have every fan feeling confident about not only his future, but his ability to contribute now.
Spencer Jones' performance against lefties has Yankees well-positioned for playoffs vs. Red Sox
Overall, Jones is hitting .259/.331/.452 with 10 homers on the season. He's been even better since being recalled on July 22, posting a .271/.337/.490 line with eight of his 10 homers coming during this most recent span.
There should be no more doubt that he should start over Trent Grisham, assuming Grisham is healthy, once the playoffs roll around. A significant part of that reasoning has to do with his performance against southpaws.
Jones has learned a lot from Cody Bellinger on how to handle those tough at-bats since he's been up in the bigs and the star left fielder has been healthy.
“When we are in the dugout, he’s one of those people I can go up to and ask, like, ‘Yo, what did you see?’ He’ll tell me bluntly what he saw, how he saw it, and essentially what he’s going to do next time. It’s like, all right, good to know before I go even into my first (at-bat) what this MVP is going to do for his first at-bat. It’s pretty sweet knowing that I’ve got these guys to help me out,” Jones said to The Athletic this week.
He couldn't have a better mentor. Bellinger isn't hitting lefties as much as he did last year, when he put up an insane .353/.415/.601 line, but his .287/.346/.449 performance in 2026 is plenty good, and better than what he's done against righties. In fact, Bellinger is about as balanced as they come with an .804 career OPS against left-handers and an .819 mark against righties.
We spoke about Rice earlier, but the early-season drama about his usage against lefties is a thing of the past. While he has more pop against righties, Rice's .255/.330/.457 line against southpaws is more than serviceable.
Despite having so many lefties in the lineup on a daily basis, the Yankees as a whole don't suffer much from it. The club is hitting a collective .247/.318/.422 against left-handed pitching this season, with a .740 OPS that ranks ninth. Remember, for most of that time, Aaron Judge hasn't been a factor, either.
Looking ahead, the Yankees' most likely opponent in the Wild Card series is the Red Sox, who are loaded with left-handers. In the rotation, they boast southpaws Payton Tolle and Ranger Suárez, with their being a possibility that Jake Bennett makes the cut, too. In the bullpen, they'll hope to unleash Garrett Crochet, Erik Miller and old friend Aroldis Chapman.
However, rather than being overmatched, we might say that this plays into the Yankees' hands. New York can handle left-handed pitching, and those lefty bats can tee off against righties. Jones emerging as a threat against southpaws only solidifies the strength and gives the Yankees another regular who doesn't need a platoon partner, allowing them to match up only where they're vulnerable.

item.content:encoded:
The Scotch Babe Ruth Reached For When He Wanted A Drink
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
Babe Ruth was as legendary for his pitching as he was for his hitting, becoming one of the "First Five" baseball players inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame. Ruth's notoriety extended off the field as well, where he was known for excessive drinking and partying. Those aren't unique interests for professional athletes these days, but Ruth's career spanned from 1914 to 1935 — Prohibition in the United States was in effect from 1920 to 1934. The 18th Amendment was no match for the Bambino, however. In the book "The Big Bam: The Life and Times of Babe Ruth," biographer Leigh Montville wrote, "Beer and Scotch and hot dogs were his nutritional supplement of choice" (via The Washington Post). His Scotch of choice was Dewar's.
In 1992, Ruth's former Yankees teammate Charlie Devens recounted how Ruth downed a whole quart of whisky while traveling by train between Boston and New York (via Los Angeles Times). Although Ruth reportedly started drinking beer as a child, Scotch was his go-to drink throughout much of his life. His daughter Dorothy recalled that he "would drink a highball, smoke a cigar and chew tobacco—all at the same time" in her book, "My Dad, the Babe." In a 2014 interview with CBS News, Ruth's daughter Julia specified that Dewar's was his favorite. Dewar's invented the highball in 1892, and Ruth undoubtedly had history with the brand, seeing as he worked at his father's saloon for a time at the beginning of his baseball career.
Dewar's and Babe Ruth have connections to one another's industries
Dewar's relationship with American sports didn't start or end with Babe Ruth. Sir Thomas Dewar, the son of Dewar's founder, was a huge soccer fan and donated the original trophy for the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open, America's oldest ongoing national soccer competition. The trophy still bears his name — The Dewar Cup. In 2021, Dewar's became the official Scotch of the U.S. Open golf championship. The latter connection feels particularly appropriate for Ruth, who was an avid golfer and outdoorsman in addition to being a prolific baseball player.
While Dewar's was Ruth's favorite Scotch, his name has found its way onto another liquor brand's bottle nearly a century after his playing days. In 2024, Remus Bourbon partnered with Ruth's family to create Babe Ruth Reserve, a limited-edition whiskey that combined three separate bourbon mash bills — a nod to Ruth's No.3 Yankees jersey. Babe Ruth Reserve had an initial release of 10,624 bottles, corresponding to Ruth's plate appearances. A subsequent release of 8,399 bottles in 2025 represented his career at-bats.
Funnily enough, Remus Bourbon is named for George Remus, known as "The King of Bootleggers," for his Prohibition-era sales of illegal liquor. It's a fitting connection to Ruth's legacy. Nearly a century later, the Bambino is still readily associated with the booze-soaked world of Prohibition when, whiskey was still America's drink of choice.
